# Liquid Software
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/
Status: published
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Liquid Software

Information provides continuity. Human decisions define the boundaries.

## Start with your perspective

Read a general introduction or explore what the resource means for your role. Each guide includes a focused summary, a reading path and a prompt to give your agent.

- [General understanding](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/general/): Understand the foundations, how the ideas fit together and what remains to be tested.
- [Business leaders](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/business-leaders/): Examine earlier accepted value, durable organizational knowledge, delegation and the ability to change direction.
- [Finance and investment](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/finance-investment/): Compare feasible strategies using future demand, timing, full lifecycle costs, uncertainty and reversibility.
- [Product and engineering](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/product-engineering/): Understand stable meaning, evolving contracts, contextual interfaces and selective agent, software and hybrid realizations.
- [Data and knowledge](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/data-knowledge/): Separate appropriate source preservation from processing investment, then assess discovery, freshness and retrieval demand.
- [Governance and policy](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/governance-policy/): Examine represented principals, delegated freedom, accountability and obligations that must survive adaptation.
- [Research and education](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/research-education/): Separate conceptual proposals, source lineage and illustrative examples, and frame comparisons that can test the claims.

You can also open the [general agent prompt](https://valto.github.io/liquid/agents/) or [compare the reading paths](https://valto.github.io/liquid/start/).

## Reverse the dependency

The digital world has often organized information and activity around what existing software can support. Liquid Software explores the reverse relationship: preserve attributable information, establish meaningful authority and shared semantics, then let interfaces and implementations take shape around actual needs.

<div class="foundations"><div><span>01</span><h3>Information</h3><p>Preserve evidence, ownership and continuity.</p></div><div><span>02</span><h3>Human decisions</h3><p>Define purpose, guidance and delegated freedom.</p></div><div><span>03</span><h3>Intelligence</h3><p>Interpret needs within shared meaning and authority.</p></div><div><span>04</span><h3>Software</h3><p>Emerge, adapt, stabilize and retire when useful.</p></div></div>

## A connected body of work

Liquid Software is both the public entry point and a specific paradigm. Adaptive interfaces, preservation for unknown future value, evolving retrieval and degrees of decision freedom each have independent value. They can be adopted separately and composed when their boundaries fit.

The conceptual framing is supplied by **Valto Loikkanen**. The writing and research are AI-assisted. The work proposes an architectural direction and testable questions; it does not claim that the full vision has been deployed or independently validated.

Start with [Beyond the Constraints of Software](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/00-beyond-the-constraints-of-software/), the supplied umbrella paper. The [whitepaper library](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/) also contains all sixteen complete research drafts, numbered 00–15.

The [33-page expanded economics paper, version 3.0](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/v3/) and [Capability Economics](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/) examine cumulative net value, time to value, lifecycle costs and reversible implementation choices.

The [Continuous Intelligence companion](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/) adds review cycles, learning about the learning process, parallel versions, selective reasoning compilation and customer outcome verification. Its principle is **continuous intelligence, adaptive evolution, stable operation and experience**. Read the complete supplied PDF or Markdown with diagrams, then explore six related concept papers independently.

## Explore and maintain

This repository is the public source for the project. Definitions, examples and related research remain attributable and independently versioned. See [principles](https://valto.github.io/liquid/principles/), the [glossary](https://valto.github.io/liquid/glossary/) and [attribution](https://valto.github.io/liquid/about/).

Maintainers can find build, validation and release instructions in the [maintenance guide](https://github.com/valto/liquid/blob/main/MAINTENANCE.md).

# Core concepts
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/
Status: published
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Core concepts

These concepts describe different parts of the transition. Liquid Software concerns changing implementations; adaptive interfaces concern interaction; information preservation concerns what survives; and decision freedom concerns the authority within which choices can change.

Each definition is a research draft with its own scope, version, relationships and associated papers. The concepts are proposals for examination and testing, rather than normative requirements for every system.

Release v0.2.0 adds a ninth concept, Capability Economics, and revises five related concepts using the expanded economics source. Their earlier public versions remain attributable to v0.1.0.

Release v0.3.0 incorporates the 33-page Economics of Execution v3 source, expands Capability Economics and Adaptive Information Retrieval, clarifies the source-attributed maturity terms and adds an optional capability decision record. Earlier paper editions and concept versions remain retained in the publication history.

Release v0.4.0 adds six concepts developed from the supplied [Continuous Intelligence companion](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/): Layered Intelligence Cycles, Meta-Learning, Stability-Aware Evolution, Parallel Realizations, Reasoning Compilation and Outcome Verification. They complement the earlier nine concepts. Learning, release and adoption can happen at different rates; useful adaptation can preserve a familiar experience.


---

# Liquid Software
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/liquid-software/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Liquid Software

**Definition.** Implementations emerge, adapt, stabilize and retire around actual needs, within durable semantics and human-defined boundaries.

Software fluidity concerns the implementation of a capability. Meaning, accepted commitments, information ownership and authority must remain understandable as that implementation changes.

UI on the fly and backend on the fly describe creation or adaptation in response to context. Liquid Software extends the principle to integrations, retrieval and execution. A deterministic implementation can remain the best choice for years; fluidity includes choosing stability.

## A reversible lifecycle

A novel need may be fulfilled intelligently. Recurring demand can justify a validated query, cache, service or other optimization. Changed needs may require adaptation. Declining demand may justify retiring that realization while preserving the promised capability or deliberately revising its commitment.

Direct execution, reusable skills, deterministic functions, modules and dedicated software form a reversible continuum, not a mandatory maturity progression. Different operations can occupy different points at the same time. Modularity supports that choice when its coordination, interface and assurance costs are justified.

Materialization fixes assumptions about workflows, data, interaction and rules. Evaluate the flexibility it removes along with the performance it gains. Independent functions and permitted alternative paths can keep exceptions workable without silently revising the capability's commitments.

## Examine the tradeoff

Measure quality, latency, cost, reliability, reversibility and the effort needed to preserve meaning. Changing software is useful when it improves fulfillment, not merely because generation is available.

Use cumulative net value, including time to value and the full lifecycle, to compare feasible realizations. Least-cost selection is sufficient only when outcomes, timing and relevant risks are comparable. Changed needs can justify evolving or dissolving an implementation while retaining source continuity.


## Evolve without forcing continuous change

Sensing, learning, reviewing, releasing and adopting can proceed at different rates. A system can learn continuously while keeping a proven interface or process stable. [Stability-Aware Evolution](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/stability-aware-evolution/) compares future outcomes together with disruption and transition costs.

[Parallel Realizations](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/parallel-realizations/) allows a candidate to be tested, released to a bounded context or retained alongside an existing version. Release, adoption and retirement are separate decisions. Multiple active versions can be justified by different tasks and preferences, subject to compatibility and support costs.

## Read further

[Research draft 04](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/04-liquid-software/) develops this concept, examples, limits and research questions.

[Capability Economics](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/) and the [expanded economics paper, version 2.0](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/) develop this reversible decision process.

The [Continuous Intelligence companion](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/) develops the temporal dimension and its evidence limits.


---

# The Adaptive Interface
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/adaptive-interface/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# The Adaptive Interface

**Definition.** Presentation and interaction respond to what is needed, by whom, where and why; how is a contextual result.

Information exists independently of one screen, document, dashboard or request format. The interface is selected or generated around the recipient, purpose, environment and nature of the information.

A human may use speech, a diagram or text; an agent may use natural language or a structured request. These can express related needs while preserving their distinct requirements for accessibility, precision and authority.

## Languages and formats

Begin with how participants express needs and carry information. Shared terminology and commitments guide interpretation. A schema can be generated, inferred or negotiated where useful; recognizable syntax alone does not establish agreed meaning.

## Preserve the relationship

Changing presentation does not confer new permission or alter the underlying commitment. Test comprehension, task outcomes, accessibility, uncertainty and the ability to move between representations without losing relevant evidence.


## Contextual, personally composed and stable

The companion distinguishes focused, dense expert, hybrid composed and primarily agent-used experiences. These modes serve different contexts; they are not stages every user must climb. The subset useful to one person can differ from another's, so aggregate low feature use does not justify identical removal for everyone.

A personally composed workspace should remain familiar and inspectable. Retain, preview, accept, reject, revert and combine are useful forms of control where the task and obligations permit them. Inferred preferences are evidence to examine, not permission for forced rearrangement, disclosure or upselling.

Implementation and experience can change independently: a stable screen can use an improved backend, and a new presentation can share the existing capability. [Parallel Realizations](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/parallel-realizations/) makes this separation explicit while accounting for compatibility and continuing support.

## Read further

[Research draft 05](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/05-the-adaptive-interface/) develops this concept, examples, limits and research questions.

[Continuous Intelligence, chapter 6](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/source/) extends it with stable contextual experiences. The original source and its figures remain available separately.


---

# Capture for Unknown Future Value
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capture-for-unknown-future-value/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Capture for Unknown Future Value

**Definition.** Preserve appropriate source richness before anticipated questions determine the full extent of what remains.

A selected field or summary can be useful while failing to preserve evidence needed for an unforeseen question. Appropriate originals retain possibilities for later interpretation and reprocessing.

Text, documents, images, audio, spatial observations and sensor information offer different evidence. No sensor combination captures all reality. Preservation is governed by purpose, consent, rights, retention and practical resources.

## Evidence and interpretation

Keep an original observation distinct from an inferred assertion and a derived index. Structured facts can themselves be authoritative when they originate as structured records. SQL is useful; the concern is losing evidence by retaining only anticipated fields.

## Separate preservation from processing investment

Retaining an appropriate original can preserve future options without immediately generating every summary, embedding, index or graph. Select processing and caching around actual demand and commitments, including sufficient metadata and security to make discovery practical.

Count preservation costs, rights, retention and future reprocessing alongside useful retrieval value. Retiring a derived optimization does not confer permission to delete its source. This distinction supports selective investment; it is not a claim that all information should be collected or that all upfront processing is unnecessary.

## Test future usefulness

Ask new questions against retained evidence, record what can and cannot be concluded, and compare the value and cost of preservation. Visible bird behavior, for example, may support an observation without establishing actual health.


## Read further

[Research draft 06](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/06-capture-for-unknown-future-value/) develops this concept, examples, limits and research questions.

[Capability Economics](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/) and page 7 of the [expanded economics paper](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/) extend the distinction between source continuity and processing expense.


---

# Adaptive Information Retrieval
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/adaptive-information-retrieval/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Adaptive Information Retrieval

**Definition.** Interpret emerging questions and evolve retrieval structures around observed needs while preserving source evidence and agreed meaning.

Retrieval can combine precise queries, indexes, graphs, semantic search and intelligent interpretation. The system chooses an appropriate path for the current question and evidence.

Repetition may justify a more efficient derived structure. The index remains distinct from the information and accepted assertions it serves. Better retrieval cannot recreate source evidence that was never retained.

## Continuity across methods

Changing the retrieval method should preserve purpose, permission, freshness, provenance and uncertainty. A response derived from several sources must make its evidential limits clear.

## Invest in processing around demand

Preserving appropriate source material does not require preprocessing every possible interpretation. Processing on retrieval, caching, selective preprocessing and broader preprocessing are reversible choices. Compare their value and complete costs, including discovery, minimum metadata, authorization, freshness, invalidation and rebuilding.

Some preparation is necessary before a source can be found or accessed safely. Within those constraints, observed need can justify a specific derived structure. Retiring that structure does not authorize deleting source evidence or pending unaccepted work, and its location does not confer canonical authority.

## An illustrative retrieval investment

The supplied Economics of Execution v3, page 23, assumes €1,300 for full extraction and horizon upkeep, then €0.01 per relevant-document retrieval, against €0.20 for on-demand extraction. At 1,000 retrievals the costs are €1,310 and €200; at 10,000 they are €1,400 and €2,000. Equal cost occurs at 6,842.105… retrievals, so the first whole count favoring preprocessing is 6,843. These are explanatory assumptions, not measured retrieval prices or demonstrated performance.

Basic indexing and access controls are already available equally to both paths. Retrieval events are distinct from archive size and unique-document count; repeat demand can instead justify selective caching. Necessary discovery, freshness, accessibility and protective controls remain costs and requirements of either approach. The original source's rounded approximately 6,842 wording is preserved in its PDF and transcription.

## Validate the change

Compare correctness, total cost, latency and recovery across existing, intelligent and hybrid paths. Include exact readback, missing evidence, changed source revisions and retirement of derived optimizations.

## Reuse understanding with its basis

Persisting evidence, propositions, assessments and decisions can reduce repeated reconstruction. Keep their assumptions, dependencies, confidence, scope and last review so a changed source or condition can invalidate the affected interpretation. Retained understanding remains revisable; a summary does not become an unquestionable fact.

The [Continuous Intelligence companion](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/) cites Optivian's maintained deal-context example. Its reported token reduction illustrates a possible preprocessing benefit, rather than independently establishing universal superiority. Preparation, updates, coverage, raw-source access and accepted answer quality belong in the comparison alongside query costs.


## Read further

[Research draft 07](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/07-adaptive-information-retrieval/) develops this concept, examples, limits and research questions.

[Capability Economics](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/) and page 7 of the [expanded economics paper](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/) develop demand-driven processing investment.

The [33-page version 3.0](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/v3/), pages 22–23, expands that reasoning and supplies the worked example above.


---

# Intelligence First, Software Second
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/intelligence-first/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Intelligence First, Software Second

**Definition.** Establish the ability to understand and fulfill a need before choosing where dedicated software provides a useful optimization.

An intelligent system can attempt a new task using available information and capabilities. Observed demand and operational requirements can then justify deterministic code or another specialized realization.

This is a change in sequencing, not an assertion that intelligence always performs better. Real-time behavior, safety-critical controls and explicit contractual guarantees can justify stable software from the outset.

## Compare fulfillment paths

Existing software, direct intelligent execution and hybrid approaches have different costs, risks and strengths. Choose using meaningful outcomes rather than the novelty of a generation technique.

Compare cumulative net value over the relevant horizon, including time to the first accepted outcome, setup, assurance, maintenance, transition, failure and foregone opportunities. Runtime price alone omits much of this decision. Count delayed benefits consistently so the same loss is not deducted again as opportunity cost.

Where direct execution is feasible, it can deliver value and reveal requirements while selective development proceeds in parallel. Both inference and software-production costs change; neither direction guarantees that specialization will repay its investment. The execution continuum is reversible, rather than a maturity sequence every capability must complete.

## A bounded experiment

Start with one capability and preserved evidence. Define accepted results and authority, compare candidate paths, and test whether specialization improves performance while retaining the same meaning and commitments.


## Read further

[Research draft 02](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/02-intelligence-first-software-second/) develops this concept, examples, limits and research questions.

[Capability Economics](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/) and the [expanded economics paper, version 2.0](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/) develop the full decision model and its evidence limits.


---

# Degrees of Decision Freedom
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/degrees-of-decision-freedom/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Degrees of Decision Freedom

**Definition.** Higher-level decisions define the contextual space in which humans and delegated actors can make further choices.

Decisions occur within existing rights, commitments, resources, circumstances and prior decisions. A principal can establish objectives and limits without prescribing every subsequent operational choice.

Freedom has several dimensions. An agent may have wide freedom to select a retrieval method, limited authority to commit money and no authority to disclose particular information. The same contextual distinction applies to people in organizations.

## Make prior decisions usable

Durable guidance, permissions and capability requirements can represent accumulated decisions. Delegation needs understandable scope, revision, traceability and escalation when a reserved decision or unresolved conflict arises.

## Evaluate meaningful control

Measure whether outcomes remain aligned with the principal, whether boundaries are understood and enforced, and whether intervention or revocation works. Human sovereignty does not require separate approval of every already-authorized operation.


## Read further

[Research draft 03](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/03-degrees-of-decision-freedom/) develops this concept, examples, limits and research questions.


---

# The Self-Optimizing Information System
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/self-optimizing-system/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# The Self-Optimizing Information System

**Definition.** Observe actual fulfillment and propose useful changes to implementations and retrieval structures under explicit authority.

The system observes semantic requests, cost, latency, correctness, sensitivity and dependencies. An optimizer can identify candidates for specialization, adaptation, consolidation or retirement.

A scheduled optimization process is an example of operational organization, not a required nightly ritual. Frequency is one signal alongside commitments and total operating costs.

## Preserve acceptance and recovery

An optimization must retain the authority, meaning and evidence requirements of the original capability. Test representative queries, source freshness and rollback. Retiring a realization does not automatically authorize withdrawing a promised capability.

## Measure net benefit

Include the expense of generating, reviewing, operating and retiring an optimization. Compare it with the intelligent or existing path and retain a suitable fallback where the commitment requires one.

The objective is cumulative net value over a relevant horizon, subject to accepted quality, risk and authority. Include time to value, enabling intelligence, adoption and restoration, maintenance, flexibility and foregone opportunities. A lower runtime bill can conceal delayed or lost value. Use least-cost selection only when outcomes and timing are comparable.

Compare plausible demand and failure scenarios with existing tools, direct agents and hybrids. Optimization can apply to a capability's meaningful contract or to its internal operations; smaller components do not automatically become separate capabilities. Reassessment may justify keeping the current realization, selectively materializing another one or retiring an unneeded derived structure.


## Learning and change have different rates

[Layered Intelligence Cycles](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/layered-intelligence-cycles/) distinguishes review purpose and depth from cadence. [Meta-Learning](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/meta-learning/) evaluates missed signals, false triggers, review costs and reversals, including whether the optimizer changes too much or too little.

A trigger calls for examination within its scope. It does not automatically authorize production change. Candidate development, release, adoption and retirement can be separate decisions. The optimizer can recommend retaining a stable realization when transition effects outweigh improvement.

Measure internal throughput and external fitness together. [Outcome Verification](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/outcome-verification/) returns to the beneficiary's original need; a completed task or lower inference bill is insufficient evidence that the problem improved.

## Read further

[Research draft 08](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/08-the-self-optimizing-information-system/) develops this concept, examples, limits and research questions.

[Capability Economics](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/) and the [expanded economics paper, version 2.0](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/) extend the comparison across time and realization granularity.

The [Continuous Intelligence companion](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/) develops these review and evolution distinctions as proposals rather than deployed optimizer behavior.


---

# Documentation as Executable Foundations
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/documentation-as-foundations/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Documentation as Executable Foundations

**Definition.** Shared terminology, capability requirements and guidance preserve meaning while implementations and operational choices evolve.

Documentation describes purpose, boundaries, accepted outcomes, terminology and relevant unknowns. Agents can use these foundations to interpret needs without requiring every implementation to be designed in advance.

Guidance is not automatically permission. A capability's documentation and the actor's actual authority answer related but distinct questions. Contradictions and unresolved meanings should remain visible.

## Maintain meaningful scope

Minimum Logical Element (MLE) is a scope discipline: a unit retains enough context to be understood across relevant perspectives. Capability Requirements Documents (CRDs) document meaningful capabilities independently of one endpoint, screen or realization.

## Verify the foundation

Test whether different participants interpret a capability consistently, whether accepted outcomes can be checked, and whether revisions preserve attributable history. Documentation helps govern adaptation without guaranteeing correctness merely by existing.


## Document learning and implementation separately

Retain the basis of an assessment: evidence, assumptions, confidence, dependencies, scope and last review. A review charter can describe purpose, depth, cadence, triggers and authority. These logical records make understanding reusable and revisable without requiring one storage schema.

Capability requirements, Skill instructions, agent orchestration and executable logic describe different concerns. The proposed [Reasoning Compilation](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/reasoning-compilation/) capability converts formally checkable portions into validated structures, preserving their assumptions and invalidation conditions. Its documentation does not establish that a compiler or Skill is installed.

## Read further

[Research draft 10](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/10-documentation-as-executable-foundations/) develops this concept, examples, limits and research questions.

The [Continuous Intelligence source, chapters 2, 7 and 9](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/source/) develops persistent understanding, compilation and proposed review/version records.


---

# Capability Economics
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Capability Economics

**Definition.** Compare feasible ways of fulfilling a capability by the risk-adjusted cumulative net value they deliver over time, including their full lifecycle and the flexibility they retain or remove.

Conceptual source: **Valto Loikkanen**, *Liquid Software: The Economics of Execution*, versions 2.0 and 3.0, 27 November 2026. This revision incorporates the expanded v3 source. The explanation, models and examples are AI-assisted elaborations, with supplied v3 scenarios identified separately. They are proposals for measurement, not empirical validation of the framework.

## Begin with the outcome

Specify the need, its beneficiary, accepted results, quality, latency, reliability, safety and authority. A path outside these boundaries is infeasible even if its runtime price is attractive. Some capabilities require a deterministic control or a validated process before first use. Others can be fulfilled using existing tools and intelligent execution while the need is still being understood.

Compare direct agents, existing software or SaaS, reusable skills, deterministic functions, modules, dedicated applications and hybrids. Include a feasible manual path or doing nothing when either is a real alternative. Intelligence itself has enabling costs: permissions, context, tools, evaluation, runtime setup and human supervision.

The useful unit is the capability or meaningful contract. Internal operations can use different realizations without becoming independent promises. CRD's capability/realization separation supplies a documentation approach; it does not prove the economics of any particular implementation.

## Compare value over the relevant horizon

A simple accounting model makes the comparison explicit:

```text
NetValue(r, scenario) =
    discounted value actually delivered over the horizon
  − enabling, building, operating, assuring and maintaining costs
  − adaptation, transition, restoration and retirement costs
  − attributable failure and rigidity losses not already counted
```

Here `r` is a candidate realization or sequence of realizations. Select among feasible candidates using plausible demand and failure scenarios, the principal's risk tolerance and required commitments. An expected value alone may conceal an unacceptable downside; explicit constraints remain part of selection.

Time matters because a benefit received later may be worth less, arrive after a market window, or never occur. A delayed benefit already absent from the value term must not be subtracted again as opportunity cost. Likewise, avoid counting failure losses both through an unsuccessful scenario and a second blanket risk deduction. Account consistently for scarce people, capital and existing resources; sunk expenditure is distinct from avoidable future cost.

Minimum cost is an adequate objective only when outcomes, timing and relevant risks are comparable. Where benefits differ, choose on net value. The v2 page 6 least-cost wording therefore needs the outcome comparability established on its page 3; v3 makes the net-value objective explicit throughout.

## Make scenarios and timing explicit

V3 page 25 proposes an expected discounted-value objective. Using different variable names to distinguish a strategy from a discount rate:

```text
V(j) = sum over scenarios s of p(s) ×
       sum over periods t of [B(j,s,t) − C(j,s,t) − L(j,s,t)] / (1 + d)^t
```

`j` is a feasible realization or staged strategy; `p(s)` is a scenario probability, with the probabilities summing to one. `B` is attributable benefit, `C` is full incremental lifecycle and transition cost, and `L` is failure or rigidity loss not already represented in the other terms. `d` is the discount rate for the chosen period. State the horizon, timing, units and any residual value consistently. This is an accounting proposal rather than an implemented optimizer.

Compare serving now and specializing later with building first, retaining existing tools and other feasible sequences. Demand observed at one stage can change a later decision. A staged strategy must have a safe initial path and an acceptable transition; it cannot assume those prerequisites away. Average expected value does not excuse unacceptable severe downside. Unknown probabilities and flexibility costs may need ranges, qualitative judgments or hard constraints rather than invented precision.

Serving a need before committing to construction can preserve options to defer, expand, alter or abandon the investment. Waiting can also forfeit value or violate a requirement. The benefit of this evidence-first sequence is conditional, and neither delay nor initial agentic fulfillment is always preferable.

## A hypothetical example: value during development

The following dollar example was developed for the v2-derived explanation. It is distinct from the supplied v3 euro example that follows.

Assume a service produces $100 of value per active day. An agent path needs $100 of setup and costs $20 per active day, starting on day 1. A dedicated implementation costs $3,000 to build, becomes available after 40 days and costs $2 per active day. Both deliver equal accepted quality. Demand lasts 90 days.

For this illustration only, ignore discounting and uncertainty. Treat the stated costs as complete for the horizon, with no separate retirement expenditure or residual value. In the hybrid, development can run in parallel with the agent service without extra shared-resource costs. These assumptions are deliberately simple and are not measured performance or market prices.

| Path | Value delivered | Total cost | Net value over 90 days |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Agent throughout | $9,000 | $100 + 90 × $20 = $1,900 | $7,100 |
| Wait for software, then operate for 50 days | $5,000 | $3,000 + 50 × $2 = $3,100 | $1,900 |
| Agent for 40 days, then software for 50 | $9,000 | $100 + 40 × $20 + $3,000 + 50 × $2 = $4,000 | $5,000 |

In these assumptions, the agent path has the greatest net value. The hybrid delivers the same benefit sooner than waiting for software, but its 50 days of runtime savings do not recover the build cost. For a longer unchanged horizon `H`, the hybrid gains `$18 × (H − 40) − $3,000` relative to the agent path. It becomes preferable after roughly 207 days if all other assumptions remain true. Different demand, quality, build costs or delivery dates can reverse the result.

This example shows why lower per-execution cost does not settle the decision. It also shows that early intelligent execution does not automatically justify subsequent materialization.

## The supplied v3 example: identical software, different timing

V3 page 15 assumes both paths build the same €12,000 module over three months, paying the investment at the start. From month four, each generates €5,000 monthly contribution at €500 monthly operating cost. In the alternative path, an existing agent environment also serves the first three months, generating €4,000 monthly contribution at €1,500 operating and assurance cost.

| First six months | Software-first | Agent-first, then the same module |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial construction | −€12,000 | −€12,000 |
| Net operations in months 1–3 | €0 | €7,500 |
| Net operations in months 4–6 | €13,500 | €13,500 |
| Cumulative net value | **€1,500** | **€9,000** |

The €7,500 difference persists after both use the same software under these assumptions. The example excludes discounting and other costs, and assumes parallel fulfillment and development are feasible. It illustrates timing rather than measured agent performance or a universally optimal sequence. Early execution can be too expensive or unreliable, and observed demand might instead eliminate the later build.

Record actual attributable contribution. Hours released are not cash until converted into avoided expenditure, profitable throughput or another defined benefit. Positive discounting lowers the present value of fixed future benefits; receiving them earlier can improve value relative to receiving them later. It does not increase their value above the same undiscounted amount. Opportunity cost concerns the best feasible alternative forgone, not the sum of every imagined opportunity.

## Use break-even as a limited check

If incremental fixed software cost is `F`, the agent cost per successful execution is `a`, and software cost is `s`, the elementary cost threshold is:

```text
N = F / (a − s), when a > s
```

If `a ≤ s` and `F` is positive, this particular runtime-saving argument gives no finite break-even point. Other benefits can still justify the software.

The formula assumes comparable outcomes and ignores timing, variable demand, changing prices, failures, maintenance, transition and residual value. Count successful accepted executions and their actual retries and supervision, rather than treating token price as the whole cost. Replace the elementary threshold with a fuller scenario comparison when those omitted factors matter.

V3 pages 10 and 17 illustrate `F = €1,200` and `s = €0.10`. Agent costs of €2.50, €1.30 and €0.50 imply thresholds of 500, 1,000 and 3,000 respectively. Reducing software-production cost moves the comparison as well. These are hypothetical inputs, not predictions. A history of 500 executions is not a build trigger: decide using remaining demand and incremental future investment. Construction already paid for is sunk and must not be charged again when comparing future operation.

## Keep the continuum reversible

Direct execution, skills, deterministic functions, modules and applications can coexist in one capability. Movement toward dedicated software is not a required maturity progression. A small validated function may be the best long-term realization; a changing activity may remain agentic; a high-utilization service may justify a dedicated application from the outset.

Materialization fixes assumptions about workflow, information, interaction and rules. It can improve speed and assurance while closing alternatives. Compare that flexibility loss with the benefit gained. Expose functions where useful, retain a permitted fallback when a commitment requires one, and preserve accepted meaning when implementations change.

The earlier v2-derived explanation used **maturity bias** for treating implementation level as evidence of decision quality. V3 page 26 gives a broader formulation: current understanding and experience can limit the alternatives a decision-maker perceives. The revision below uses that source-attributed formulation while retaining the earlier warning. Neither concern makes agent use a proxy for decision quality.

## Recognize alternatives before choosing among them

V3 page 26 separates three dimensions of maturity:

| Dimension | Question |
| --- | --- |
| Understanding | Which operating paradigms and possible realizations does the decision-maker recognize? |
| Experience | Which alternatives have been tried enough to reveal their practical capabilities and limits? |
| Implementation | Which realization is actually selected for this capability? |

Its spectrum describes traditional software, AI-enabled software, agentic software, agent-first operations and AI-native operations, with unknown further paradigms explicitly left open. It is a conceptual classification rather than a validated assessment scale.

Broader understanding can lead to deliberate conventional software use. The same visible implementation can reflect informed selection or lack of awareness of alternatives. Seek practical evidence where useful and revisit assumptions; do not infer decision quality from how many agents are present. Retain durable knowledge and records when workers are instantiated or discarded. The separate named maturity paper remains unavailable to this review.

## Include adoption and reversal

An implementation can consume resources without delivering its promised value. Introducing it can require training, migration, testing and process changes. Returning to the earlier system can require a second transition, reconciliation and restoration. This is **double transition cost**, a possible exposure to examine rather than a standard multiplier to add to every budget.

The source's Pendo, GAO and UK examples concern distinct measures and populations. Underused features are not necessarily unnecessary: infrequent critical or seasonal functions may be valuable. Projects missing a cash-savings target may still provide security or other benefits. Qualitative reversal reports establish possible mechanisms, not their prevalence. None establishes a universal failure rate or proves that an agentic replacement would have succeeded.

## Apply the same reasoning to information processing

Preserving a source and preprocessing every possible interpretation are separate investments. Appropriate capture can retain future options without immediately generating every summary, index, graph or embedding.

Select among processing on retrieval, caching a useful result, preprocessing a recurring category and broader preprocessing. Include the cost of discovery, permissions, minimum metadata, freshness checks, invalidation and rebuilding. Some of this work is necessary before retrieval can be safe or practical. Demand-driven processing requires enough source discoverability to learn what is being requested.

A disposable derived structure does not change canonical source authority. Retiring it does not authorize deleting the original or pending work. Storage, privacy, retention and access commitments remain part of the feasible boundary.

Modularity can extend the comparison to models, processing and infrastructure. Count interface, integration, coordination, testing and observability overhead. Owned hardware can reduce one marginal price while adding utilization and lifecycle costs. A vendor's architectural claim needs a comparable measured workload before it supports a cost advantage.

V3 page 23 assumes €1,300 for full extraction and horizon upkeep, €0.01 per preprocessed retrieval and €0.20 per on-demand extraction. Both paths already have equivalent basic indexing and access controls. On-demand costs €200 at 1,000 retrievals, against €1,310 for preprocessing. At 10,000, the totals are €2,000 and €1,400. The continuous crossover is `1,300 / 0.19 = 6,842.105…`; preprocessing first costs less at **6,843 whole retrievals**. The source's approximately 6,842 is rounded, and its original text remains intact.

Count retrieval events separately from distinct documents. Repeated access may justify selective caching instead of full extraction. Include freshness, discovery, validation and access obligations consistently; the example does not establish that scanning raw archives on each request is efficient. Accessibility, searchability, compliance or response-time commitments can justify preparation before observed demand.

## Compose at the meaningful capability boundary

The procurement example on v3 page 21 combines a reasoning model to clarify need, a validated local model for field extraction, declared rules for policy, an exact calculation function, an authorized existing API for commitment and an authoritative evidence record. A human with the required authority handles exceptions or approves a commitment where necessary. Each replacement must satisfy its contract and governing permissions; a capability description alone grants neither spending rights nor deployment authority.

Reuse can justify specialization across different activities. V3 page 28 assumes a shared calculation used 6,000 times, costing €0.40 per agent execution or €900 fixed plus €0.02 per function execution. The totals are €2,400 and €1,020, a €1,380 saving. At 1,000 uses, €400 versus €920 does not justify a new function on this cost comparison. Its custom-request and reconciliation examples illustrate different compositions; they do not supply enough comparative data to establish an entire portfolio optimum.

Choose a meaningful unit of purpose and contract, rather than the smallest possible code fragment. Interface, versioning, discovery and dependency overhead can outweigh reuse. Compare attributable owned-model capacity with hosted execution over actual utilization, assurance and maintenance. Idle capacity is not universally free, and local placement alone does not establish privacy or reliability.

## A measurable operating loop

1. Define the capability, commitments, beneficiaries and relevant horizon.
2. Identify existing resources and feasible agentic, software, manual and hybrid paths.
3. Execute where feasible and record accepted outcomes, time, actual cost and exceptions.
4. Compare full net value and plausible demand, failure and transition scenarios.
5. Materialize selectively when the evidence justifies the investment.
6. Reassess changed needs, prices and constraints; retain, evolve or retire the realization within authority.

Evaluation should test the claim that one sequence improves fulfillment. Measure elapsed time to first accepted value, quality, successful-execution cost, cumulative benefit, implementation and restoration expenditure, and meaningful exceptions. Compare with existing tools as well as new agent paths. Keep measurement periods and demand assumptions explicit.

A useful experiment can fail: no feasible direct path may exist, demand may not repay specialization, or coordination overhead may exceed savings. Reporting such results improves selection rather than invalidating stable software as a legitimate choice.

## Keep a practical decision record

V3 page 27 proposes a lightweight record. Capture the capability identity and version, accountable owner, required outcome and acceptance criteria, existing baseline, feasible alternatives, observed and forecast demand, quality and full cost evidence, selected strategy, governing authority, review triggers and recovery path. Separate observations from estimates, and explain important unknowns rather than supplying arbitrary probabilities.

A compact [decision-record template](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/decision-record/) with [editable Markdown](https://valto.github.io/liquid/content/concepts/capability-decision-record.md) turns this into a reviewable business case. It is optional documentation, not a new CRD schema or authority grant.

The optimizer itself has lifecycle costs. Revisit a decision when demand, quality, prices, exceptions, commitments or source evidence change materially. Retain a stable realization when new generation and assessment would cost more than the likely improvement. Permission to propose a change is distinct from permission to deploy, transfer data, purchase or withdraw a service. Measure accepted value and avoided waste rather than rewarding application or agent production.

## Compare improvement with the path to it

[Stability-Aware Evolution](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/stability-aware-evolution/) adds explicit attention to familiar workflows, disruption, absorption of change and parallel upkeep. Include these effects once within the lifecycle comparison; its qualitative change heuristic is not an additional universal financial formula.

Compare internal throughput and external fitness as well as costs. A more efficient process can serve a declining need. [Parallel Realizations](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/parallel-realizations/) can preserve an accepted path while an alternative is tested or selectively adopted, but duplicated assurance, compatibility and maintenance consume resources too.

## Read further

Read the [complete economics paper and reference audit](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/). Related research drafts develop [intelligence-first sequencing](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/02-intelligence-first-software-second/), [Liquid Software](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/04-liquid-software/), [self-optimization](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/08-the-self-optimizing-information-system/) and [implementation lifecycles](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/12-the-lifecycle-of-liquid-software/).

The supplied economics v2 and [complete v3 paper](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/v3/) are this revision's conceptual sources. The earlier economics v1 and separate named AI-maturity companion were not supplied or read; the substantive maturity chapter within v3 was read in full.

# An Intelligence-Native Reference Architecture
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/architecture/
Status: published
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# An Intelligence-Native Reference Architecture

## Different concerns, different rates of change

| Concern | What persists | What may adapt |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Principal | Identity, relationships and authority | Representatives and providers |
| Information | Originals, accepted revisions and provenance | Indexes, interpretations and projections |
| Capability | Purpose, outcomes and commitments | Intelligent, deterministic and hybrid realizations |
| Interaction | Agreed meaning and disclosure boundaries | Languages, formats and contextual presentation |
| Governance | Human decisions and external obligations | Operational choices within delegated freedom |

An individual and an entity are useful information-principal anchors. The requester may still be a human, agent or application. The immediate actor, represented principal, beneficiary and purpose remain distinct.

## A bounded request

1. Identify the need, requester and represented principal.
2. Resolve meaning and actual authority using shared context and guidance.
3. Select an existing, intelligent or hybrid fulfillment path.
4. Validate the accepted outcome, evidence, freshness and uncertainty.
5. Return the suitable representation and preserve commitments.
6. Observe demand and propose improvements within the same boundaries.

## Complementary frameworks

[PIOS](https://www.peecos.org/pios/master) and [EIOS](https://github.com/entity-core/eios) provide personal and entity information-framework proposals. [PAIX](https://github.com/privateaiexchange/paix-spec) explores interaction across participants. [CRD](https://valto.github.io/crd/) documents capabilities, while [MLE](https://valto.github.io/crd/mle.html) helps preserve meaningful scope.

These are related bodies of work with their own authority and scope. Adoption of one Liquid Software concept does not require adopting every framework.

## Learning, evolution and experience

The [Continuous Intelligence companion](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/) connects signals, persistent understanding, purposeful reviews, change decisions, evolution paths and outcome verification. Feedback can revise understanding and review policies without automatically changing operations.

Review purpose and depth are independent of frequency. A scheduled review and a material event trigger can complement each other. The meta-loop examines the quality of those reviews. Changes can improve a backend beneath a stable experience, introduce a parallel alternative, or deliberately retire a realization.

The source proposes nine logical objects: a signal, review policy, review record, change proposal, CRD, implementation version, experience composition, experiment or rollout, and outcome evidence. They describe relationships to preserve rather than a mandatory database schema. Facts, inferences, proposals, approved decisions and deployed implementations retain distinct statuses.

Its decision questions are **why, what, who, how, when, verification and learning**, preceded by identifying what needs checking. They help connect purpose, authority and execution. Candidate construction, validation, release, adoption and retirement remain separate effects; a trigger does not grant them all.

[Pulse CXM](https://www.pulsecxm.com/) supplies a customer-side application context connecting signals to coordinated work and verification. EIOS covers broader organizational continuity; PIOS covers personal owner-controlled context. A personally composed interface can use an organizational capability through authorized interactions without automatically transferring personal Core information.

CRD preserves capability meaning; Skills guide use; agents orchestrate; software or declared structures implement suitable parts. The proposed Reasoning Compilation Skill has its own requirements and governance. Describing this arrangement does not establish its implementation or authorize a deployment.

## Examine the integrated model

This is a reference architecture for testing. It is not a deployed system or a new mandatory protocol. [Research draft 15](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/15-the-architecture-of-an-intelligence-native-world/) develops the boundaries and research questions. [Draft 14](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/14-from-software-centric-to-information-centric-computing/) addresses transition from existing systems.


---

# Principles
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/principles/
Status: published
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Principles

## Preserve attributable information

Retain appropriate source evidence, accepted revisions and provenance. Distinguish an original, an interpretation and a derived retrieval structure. Preservation remains governed by purpose, rights and resources.

## Keep meaningful human authority

Make delegation, prior decisions and reserved choices understandable. Technical availability is not permission. Operational autonomy stays within the principal's actual authority and applicable commitments.

## Let context determine interaction

What is needed, by whom, where and why guide how information is presented and exchanged. Languages and formats carry needs and information; shared meaning guides interpretation.

## Separate capability from realization

A capability's purpose and accepted outcome can persist through different implementations. Changing or retiring code does not silently change a commitment or erase the information it serves.

## Prefer useful adaptation

Create, retain or retire software using observed need and measured benefit. Stable implementations remain legitimate choices. Include quality, reliability, cost, recovery and uncertainty in the comparison.

## Keep proposals testable and attributable

Distinguish established technology, related prior work, the conceptual synthesis and experiments. Preserve corrections and source versions. Agreement between AI-assisted summaries is not independent empirical corroboration.

## Compare cumulative value over time

Choose feasible realizations by accepted outcomes and cumulative net value, including time to value, full lifecycle costs, risk, transitions and retained flexibility. Cost minimization assumes comparable benefits and timing. Avoid counting the same opportunity or failure loss twice.

## Invest selectively in processing

Preserve appropriate sources and choose processing, caching and preprocessing around demand, freshness and commitments. Include necessary discovery and security work. Retiring a derived structure does not change source authority or authorize source deletion.

These economic and processing principles are developed from [The Economics of Execution, version 2.0](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/).

## Separate learning from forced change

Sensing, understanding, reviewing, releasing and adopting can proceed at different rates. Define review purpose, depth, cadence and triggers. Evaluate the learning process itself, including missed signals and unnecessary disruption.

## Give stable experience value

Compare future outcomes together with transitions, familiarity, switching and support costs. Retain an accepted realization or offer a parallel alternative when justified. Contextual modes and personal compositions need not converge on one expert interface.

## Compile only checkable portions

Validate formally expressible logic independently, retain its assumptions and define invalidation. Deterministic execution is insufficient evidence of truth, completeness or freshness.

## Verify the original need

Connect signals, decisions and execution to beneficiary outcomes. Consider internal throughput and external fitness. Completed tasks, feature adoption and token savings measure parts of the system; they do not alone establish sustained improvement.

These additional principles are developed from the [Continuous Intelligence companion](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/), a conceptual source with explicit research and vendor-evidence limits.


---

# Glossary
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/glossary/
Status: published
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Glossary

**Liquid Software:** implementations that can emerge, adapt, stabilize and retire around actual needs, within durable meaning and authority.

**Information-centric:** preserving attributable information independently of one application or presentation.

**Intelligence-native:** treating interpretation and suitable fulfillment of emerging needs as an initial capability.

**Adaptive interface:** a presentation or interaction chosen around recipient, purpose, information and environment.

**Source evidence:** retained observations or records with attributable origin and relevant context.

**Accepted assertion:** a proposition accepted within an explicit authority and revision boundary; it is distinct from an unaccepted inference.

**Derived structure:** a rebuildable representation used for retrieval, interpretation or presentation. Its physical location does not confer canonical authority.

**Capability:** a meaningful ability defined through purpose, boundaries and accepted outcomes.

**Realization:** a current intelligent, deterministic or hybrid means of fulfilling a capability.

**Principal:** the individual or entity whose authority, information or interests are represented.

**Operational actor:** the human, agent or application initiating or fulfilling an interaction.

**Degrees of decision freedom:** contextual space for further choices within inherited decisions, commitments and resources.

**Shared semantics:** agreed meaning that makes an interaction interpretable; common syntax alone is insufficient.

**Schema:** a type or structural description used in an interaction. Its authorship, timing, lifetime and negotiation are distinct from validation under a particular current language.

**MLE:** Minimum Logical Element, the smallest unit that retains meaningful context across relevant perspectives.

**CRD:** Capability Requirements Document, an implementation-independent description of one contextually meaningful capability.

**PIOS / EIOS:** related proposals for personal and entity information, knowledge and continuity.

**PAIX:** Private AI Exchange, a related body of work on interaction across participants.

**Capability economics:** comparing feasible realizations through risk-adjusted cumulative net value over a relevant horizon, including full lifecycle costs and retained flexibility.

**Time to value:** elapsed time before a capability delivers an accepted useful outcome; its economic effect depends on the timing and value of those outcomes.

**Execution continuum:** reversible choices among direct intelligent execution, skills, functions, modules, applications and hybrids; not a required maturity sequence.

**Double transition cost:** the possible combined cost of adopting an unsuitable implementation and restoring or moving to another one; a scenario to assess, not a universal multiplier.

**Maturity bias:** in Economics of Execution v3, limits to perceived alternatives arising from current understanding and experience. The earlier v2-derived explanation emphasized the related mistake of judging decision quality by an implementation's position on a presumed progression. This is a source-attributed conceptual revision, not a validated assessment.

**Informed selection:** deliberately comparing recognized feasible alternatives and their limitations, supported where useful by practical experience. A conventional implementation can be the informed choice.

**Understanding, experiential and implementation maturity:** respectively, the operating alternatives a decision-maker recognizes, has practical experience with, and chooses to implement. V3 distinguishes them; visible implementation does not establish the other two.

**Evidence-driven materialization:** using demonstrated or credibly anticipated need to justify creating or stabilizing a specialized realization. Upfront requirements can justify investment before observed use.

**Premature determinism:** fixing behavior before relevant variation, exceptions and future change are sufficiently understood. It is distinct from enforcing intentional safety or authority constraints.

**Capability-level optimization:** comparing and revisiting realizations at meaningful units of purpose and contract, including reuse across activities and the cost of coordination.

**Dissolution:** retiring or replacing a realization while preserving necessary evidence and accepted commitments, or explicitly revising those commitments through proper authority.

These economic terms are developed from [The Economics of Execution, version 2.0](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/) and its [version 3.0 expansion](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/v3/). V3's maturity spectrum is a conceptual classification; the separate named maturity companion was not supplied.

**Layered intelligence cycles:** reviews with distinct purposes and depths, suitable recurring cadences and evidence-triggered exceptions. No universal daily-to-annual schedule is prescribed.

**Review charter:** the proposed description of a review's purpose, scope, evidence, depth, authority, outputs, cadence, triggers and revisit conditions.

**Persistent understanding:** retained evidence, propositions, assessments and decisions with their support and dependencies, enabling reuse and correction rather than unquestioned truth.

**Meta-learning:** in this companion, evaluating and improving the organizational learning process itself, including reviews, triggers and errors; distinct from claiming coverage of the full machine-learning literature on meta-learning.

**Stability-aware evolution:** assessing improvements together with transitions, disruption, switching, risk and continuing support, recognizing the positive value of dependable operation and familiar experience.

**Internal throughput:** valuable outputs per unit of time or resource at acceptable quality; activity counts alone do not establish it.

**External fitness:** how well outcomes continue to suit relevant customers, markets and conditions.

**Parallel realizations:** compatible alternatives serving one capability, with separate decisions about candidate validation, release, adoption and retirement.

**Release versus adoption:** making an approved version available within scope versus actually selecting and using it. Availability does not determine every user's transition.

**Experience composition:** a contextual arrangement of capabilities and presentation, potentially combining multiple providers. Focused, expert, hybrid and agent-used modes are choices rather than maturity stages.

**Reasoning compilation / crystallization:** materializing formally checkable portions of reasoning into validated structures while retaining assumptions, provenance, limits and invalidation conditions.

**Reasoning Compilation Skill:** a proposed capability that examines formalizable operations, creates and checks candidates, supports bounded comparison and monitors revalidation. Describing it does not mean it has been installed.

**Outcome verification:** examining whether the beneficiary's original need improved, connecting signals, decisions, execution and lived results. Task completion is partial evidence.

**Pulse CXM:** the named customer-side application context for signals, coordinated actions, execution and verified improvement; complementary to broader EIOS organizational continuity and PIOS personal context.

These additional terms are developed from [Continuous Intelligence, Adaptive Evolution, and Stable Experience](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/), version 1.0, 28 November 2026. They are source-attributed proposals rather than a new mandatory protocol or evidence of the complete architecture's deployment.


---

# Research and related work

## An attributable synthesis

Valto Loikkanen supplies the conceptual direction. The conversation, supplied umbrella paper and AI-assisted research drafts develop a connected argument; they do not constitute independent empirical validation of one another.

## Related original work

- **A Vision of Liquid Software; associated book Liquid Software: How to Achieve Trusted Continuous Updates in the DevOps World** — JFrog; related book by Fred Simon, Yoav Landman and Baruch Sadogursky. Associated book copyright 2018. [Original source](https://jfrog.com/whitepaper/a-vision-of-liquid-software/).

- **Malleable Software: Restoring User Agency in a World of Locked-Down Apps** — Geoffrey Litt, Josh Horowitz, Peter van Hardenberg and Todd Matthews. June 2025. [Original source](https://www.inkandswitch.com/essay/malleable-software/).

- **Local-first software: You own your data, in spite of the cloud** — Martin Kleppmann, Adam Wiggins, Peter van Hardenberg and Mark McGranaghan. Web essay April 2019; Onward! October 2019, pp. 154–178; DOI 10.1145/3359591.3359737. [Original source](https://www.inkandswitch.com/essay/local-first/).

- **Dynamicland FAQ** — Dynamicland Foundation. Living page in /2024/; accessed 26 November 2026. [Original source](https://dynamicland.org/2024/FAQ/).

- **GraphQL Specification** — GraphQL Foundation / specification contributors. September 2025 edition, selected explicitly. [Original source](https://spec.graphql.org/September2025/).

- **Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures, Chapter 5: Representational State Transfer** — Roy Thomas Fielding. Doctoral dissertation, 2000. [Original source](https://ics.uci.edu/~fielding/pubs/dissertation/rest_arch_style.htm).

- **PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model** — W3C Provenance Working Group. W3C Recommendation, 30 April 2013. [Original source](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/).

- **A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks** — E. F. Codd. Communications of the ACM 13(6), June 1970, pp. 377–387; DOI 10.1145/362384.362685. [Original source](https://www.seas.upenn.edu/~zives/03f/cis550/codd.pdf).

- **No Silver Bullet: Essence and Accidents of Software Engineering** — Frederick P. Brooks, Jr.. UNC technical report TR86-020, September 1986. [Original source](https://www.cs.unc.edu/techreports/86-020.pdf).

- **End-to-End Arguments in System Design** — J. H. Saltzer, D. P. Reed and D. D. Clark. ACM Transactions on Computer Systems 2(4), November 1984, pp. 277–288. [Original source](https://web.mit.edu/Saltzer/www/publications/endtoend/endtoend.pdf).

- **Malleable software in the age of LLMs** — Geoffrey Litt. March 2023. [Original source](https://www.geoffreylitt.com/2023/03/25/llm-end-user-programming).

- **The Case for Learned Index Structures** — Tim Kraska, Alex Beutel, Ed H. Chi, Jeffrey Dean and Neoklis Polyzotis. arXiv:1712.01208v3, 30 April 2018. [Original source](https://arxiv.org/html/1712.01208v3).

- **OAuth 2.0 Rich Authorization Requests** — Torsten Lodderstedt, Justin Richer and Brian Campbell. RFC 9396, May 2023. [Original source](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9396.html).

- **MyLifeBits — project overview and publication list** — Microsoft Research; Gordon Bell, Jim Gemmell and Roger Lueder. Project established 2 November 2001; overview retrieved 26 November 2026. [Original source](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/project/mylifebits/).

- **Solid Protocol** — Solid Community Group. Draft Community Group Report, 12 May 2024. [Original source](https://solidproject.org/TR/protocol).

## Sources for continuous intelligence and evolution

The supplied [Continuous Intelligence companion](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/) is a same-origin conceptual source, dated 28 November 2026. Its PDF, Markdown and diagrams are retained separately from the additional concept papers. The following primary references were assessed during this intake:

- **Pulse CXM** — Digiole. Complete rendered public overview read on 28 November 2026; describes customer signals, coordinated action and verification. No demo registration or independent product test. [Original](https://www.pulsecxm.com/).
- **Talking Products and Venues** and **PIOS & Personal Core Infrastructure** — Valto Loikkanen. Complete project pages read; same-origin project descriptions with their own scope, rather than independent deployment evidence. [Talking Products and Venues](https://valto.github.io/projects/talking-products-venues.html); [PIOS project](https://valto.github.io/projects/pios-personal-core-infrastructure.html).
- **MDIL Kide, declared reasoning and connection resources** — MDIL Labs. Complete public homepage, review summary and rendered connection overview read. Vendor-described methods and task results; the full system card and controlled evaluation materials were not read or independently replicated. The connection page's late-2026 alpha wording differs from November beta-launch wording elsewhere. [Overview](https://mdil.ai/); [review summary](https://review.mdil.ai/); [connection page](https://code.mdil.ai/connect).
- **The hidden cost of connecting AI straight to your sales stack** — Roope Heinilä, Optivian, 16 June 2026. Complete article read. Representative customer-run figures are vendor-reported; they do not establish independently matched whole-lifecycle outcomes. [Original](https://optivian.ai/insights/hidden-cost-ai-sales-stack/).
- **The 2019 Feature Adoption Report** — Pendo. Earlier complete main report and methodology assessment retained. Three-month, 615-subscription aggregate usage findings do not prescribe individual feature removal or measure every feature's value. [Original](https://www.pendo.io/resources/the-2019-feature-adoption-report/).
- **Progressive Disclosure** — Jakob Nielsen, 3 December 2006. Complete main article read; related guidance on managing visible complexity. [Original](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/progressive-disclosure/).
- **Customization Features Done Correctly for the Right Reasons** — Nielsen Norman Group. Public overview and described method read; the full 93-page report was not. Its scope is user customization rather than inferred personalization. [Overview](https://www.nngroup.com/reports/customization-features/).
- **Parallel Change** — Danilo Sato, 13 May 2014, hosted by Martin Fowler. Complete article read; expand, migrate and contract is a concrete interface-evolution precedent. [Original](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/ParallelChange.html).
- **Feature Toggles (aka Feature Flags)** — Pete Hodgson, 9 October 2017, hosted by Martin Fowler. Relevant categorization, validation and carrying-cost sections read; not the entire article. [Original](https://martinfowler.com/articles/feature-toggles.html).
- **Use a canary deployment strategy** — Google Cloud, page updated 10 November 2026. Complete main guide read; documents staged software rollout, rather than validating parallel business-model evolution. [Original](https://docs.cloud.google.com/deploy/docs/deployment-strategies/canary).
- **8 Design Guidelines for Complex Applications** — Kate Kaplan, 8 November 2020. Complete main article read; relevant guidance on complex workflows and usable capability. [Original](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/complex-application-design/).

The exact source bytes, read scopes and unresolved claims are recorded in the private source register. Extending established UX and delivery patterns into the whole proposed architecture remains a research question. Economic examples and vendor task results should retain their populations, baselines and accounting limits.

## Evidence and further work

The papers identify actual source editions and research limits. Some long works were consulted in relevant sections; cited implementation comparisons are not independent tests of the complete vision. Controlled experiments should compare quality, total effort, latency, cost, permission compliance, recovery and switching between realizations.

The [Internet beyond applications](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/13-the-internet-beyond-applications/) places the technical concepts in information-flow and economic context. Personal Application Ecosystems and loyal personal representation are complementary questions, rather than mandatory dependencies.

# About, Attribution and Citation
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/about/
Status: published
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# About, Attribution and Citation

**Conceptual source and project owner: Valto Loikkanen.**

This is an English-first body of conceptual research. AI-assisted synthesis, research and drafting develop the source discussion into independently useful definitions and papers. The attribution does not claim exclusive invention of all component ideas or priority for the established term Liquid Software.

## Suggested citation for the supplied umbrella paper

# Beyond the Constraints of Software

Status: published

# Beyond the Constraints of Software

*The transition toward an information-centric, intelligence-native world.*

Conceptual source: **Valto Loikkanen**. Conceptual White Paper 00, version 1.0, dated 26 November 2026. The supplied PDF is retained unchanged, including its AI-assisted source statement.

## The shared thesis

Information provides continuity. Human decisions define the boundaries. Intelligence fulfills needs, with software emerging as an optimization.

The paper connects four reversals: preserve appropriate source richness before storage anticipates every future question; retrieve around emerging needs; derive interfaces from context; and choose software implementations around useful capabilities.

Its twelve pages connect Liquid Software, adaptive interfaces, unknown future information value, adaptive retrieval, self-optimization, individual and entity principals, decision freedom, internet economics and practical transition questions.

## Read the original

The PDF is the original supplied edition. This page is an overview, not a replacement of its wording. A [complete text transcription](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/00-beyond-the-constraints-of-software/text/) makes every page searchable and preserves the supplied source note. The embedded diagram remains in the original PDF.

## The companion research drafts

The [sixteen-paper research collection](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/) develops distinct questions with definitions, examples, limitations, prior work and proposed experiments. Its paper 00 is a separate researched umbrella treatment. Draft 14 addresses transition; draft 15 supplies the reference architecture.
