# Liquid Software: a general introduction
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/general/
Status: reader-guide
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Liquid Software: a general introduction

Liquid Software explores a digital world in which your information and intentions outlast the tools that happen to serve them. Instead of making every useful activity wait for a dedicated application, an intelligent system can interpret a need and use an appropriate existing, agentic, deterministic or hybrid way to fulfill it.

The central question is **what should remain dependable when software can change more easily?** The answer in this resource is attributable information, understandable meaning, accepted commitments and human authority. Interfaces and execution methods can adapt around those foundations.

## Five ideas to carry into the papers

**Information provides continuity.** An appropriate original document can support a later question that its first summary did not anticipate. Preserve the distinction between evidence, an interpretation and a useful index. Ownership, consent and retention still govern what may be kept.

**A capability has meaning beyond its implementation.** Preparing a reliable commitments briefing is a meaningful ability. A screen, query or model call can help realize it. Replacing the screen should preserve what counts as an accepted commitment and whose information may be used.

**Interaction can suit the recipient.** A person might need a spoken explanation; an analyst a table; an agent structured text. Shared meaning can guide these presentations. A new format alone supplies neither agreement nor permission.

**Software is a choice to evaluate.** Repeated work can justify a validated function, cache or service. A changing task may remain intelligent. A critical control may need stable software from its first use. The proposed continuum allows all of these choices and allows them to be revisited.

**Learning need not disturb what works.** A system can notice changes and review them while keeping operations and your familiar workspace stable. A new version can be offered alongside the current one. Whether to adopt it depends on useful outcomes, transition costs and your applicable choices.

## Imagine preparing tomorrow's briefing

You ask, “Which commitments need my attention tomorrow?” A bounded system identifies you, applies the agreed meaning of commitment, checks authorized source records and returns a suitable explanation with references and uncertainty. It might combine an exact date query with intelligent interpretation of notes.

If you ask often, a validated query or cache could become worthwhile. It might improve beneath the same familiar interface. A different presentation could remain an optional alternative. The records, commitments and actual outcome still matter. This is illustrative, rather than a deployed service description.

## What changes for the reader

Ask first what outcome you want, what evidence it needs and what authority is available. Then ask which tool or combination can fulfill it acceptably. This helps separate a durable need from the features of whichever app currently handles it.

The related ideas can help separately: source preservation without generated interfaces, adaptive presentation with conventional software, or capability economics inside an existing organization. Understanding the resource does not require adopting every related framework.

## What remains to be established

The resource is conceptual and AI-assisted. Its economic figures are illustrative. A fluent answer is not proof of correctness, and software generation does not establish reliability. Useful evaluation must compare accepted outcomes, cost, latency, permission compliance and recovery against real alternatives.

## A short reading path

1. [Beyond the Constraints of Software](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/00-beyond-the-constraints-of-software/). Begin with the supplied overall argument.
2. [Liquid Software](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/liquid-software/). Understand the paradigm and reversible lifecycle.
3. [Continuous Intelligence, Adaptive Evolution, and Stable Experience](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/). Read the executive synthesis and stable-experience discussion.
4. [An Intelligence-Native Reference Architecture](https://valto.github.io/liquid/architecture/). See which concerns persist and which adapt.

## Questions to explore

- Which parts of one activity should survive a change of app or model?
- What evidence and prior decisions would let an agent understand the need?
- What should the system learn, and what would justify changing my current experience?

[Choose another perspective](https://valto.github.io/liquid/start/) when you want to examine the business, technical or governance implications.


---

# Liquid Software for business leaders
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/business-leaders/
Status: reader-guide
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Liquid Software for business leaders

Liquid Software changes the starting point for technology decisions: define the business capability and its required outcome, then select a feasible way to deliver it. An application, an agent and a hybrid workflow are possible realizations of that capability. Their usefulness depends on accepted results and the organization they serve.

For a business leader, the main question is **how can we deliver value sooner while retaining the ability to change direction?** This resource connects that question to durable knowledge, delegation and the full cost of implementation.

## Manage the outcome and the retained knowledge

A capability such as preparing a compliant supplier comparison should have an accountable owner, accepted results and explicit commitments. The organization's supplier records, terminology and prior decisions should remain understandable even if the current application or agent is replaced.

That separation can reveal useful options: use an existing service, fulfill a changing request with available tools, specialize a recurring calculation, or retain a conventional process. Counting new applications or agents does not show whether the outcome improved.

## Delegate with a clear decision boundary

Degrees of Decision Freedom describes how prior decisions establish room for subsequent choices. A team or agent can have broad freedom to find evidence and compare offers while a person retains authority to approve the purchase. A new interface or faster execution path should preserve that distinction.

This means leaders can define purpose, limits and escalation points without specifying every operational step. The organization still needs usable guidance, traceable evidence and a way to intervene when a reserved decision arises.

## Review at the depth the question needs

Daily delivery checks, weekly bottleneck reviews and strategic assessments have different purposes. Cadence and depth are independent: a market signal can justify an immediate strategic review while stable operations continue. A meta-review asks whether the organization notices the right signals and reviews them usefully.

In an illustrative supplier workflow, better calculations could improve beneath a familiar interface while a new process is evaluated in parallel. Reviewing or releasing that alternative does not itself adopt it or authorize a purchasing commitment.

## Evaluate the transition as well as the running cost

Capability Economics compares cumulative net value over a relevant horizon. Include setup, assurance, supervision, time to accepted value, maintenance, adoption and restoration if the change is reversed. A lower price per execution can coexist with a worse overall investment.

Track internal throughput and external fitness together. Efficient delivery of an unwanted offering creates little value. Verify whether the customer's original problem improved; completed tasks and new-interface adoption are partial measures. Account for the support burden of parallel versions and the value of familiar work.

## A useful management discussion

Choose one capability with a real beneficiary and measurable acceptance criteria. Identify the current baseline, feasible alternatives, sources, accountable owner and decision boundary. Ask what would justify continuing, specializing, changing or stopping the new realization, and what must be preserved if it is withdrawn.

The framework does not establish that every business should become agent-first. Existing tools, stable controls and upfront development remain legitimate choices where their outcomes and constraints justify them.

## A short reading path

1. [Capability Economics](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/). Frame feasible strategies and their full value.
2. [Degrees of Decision Freedom](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/degrees-of-decision-freedom/). Define delegated and reserved decisions.
3. [Layered Intelligence Cycles](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/layered-intelligence-cycles/). Choose useful review purposes, depth and timing.
4. [Continuous Intelligence, Adaptive Evolution, and Stable Experience](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/). Read change choices and the customer-verification loop.

## Questions to explore

- Which outcome is delayed by waiting for a new application, and is earlier fulfillment feasible?
- What organizational knowledge and commitments must survive a provider change?
- Which decisions can be delegated, and which remain reserved?
- Which customer outcomes would justify retaining, selectively adopting or retiring an alternative?

For a more detailed cost comparison, continue with the [finance and investment guide](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/finance-investment/).

# Liquid Software for finance and investment
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/finance-investment/
Status: reader-guide
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Liquid Software for finance and investment

Liquid Software treats software specialization as an investment in fulfilling a meaningful capability. The financial question is **which feasible strategy delivers the best cumulative net value, given demand, timing, uncertainty and the cost of changing course?** A low runtime price is one input to that comparison.

This perspective serves finance leaders, procurement teams and investors assessing implementation choices. It is a decision framework, rather than a valuation model or an investment recommendation.

## Compare strategies over the same horizon

Identify the accepted outcome and alternatives before estimating costs. An existing service, a manual process, direct intelligent execution, a reusable function and staged combinations may all be relevant. Quality, authority and required reliability constrain which choices are feasible.

Count benefits and costs consistently: initial enablement, development, assurance, recurring execution, supervision, adoption, upkeep and transitions. Compare the timing of accepted benefits as well as their size. If delays already reduce benefits in the model, do not deduct the same loss again as opportunity cost.

## Use break-even for the question it actually answers

The elementary threshold `N = F / (a − s)` compares fixed incremental software cost with a per-execution saving when `a > s`. With the supplied v3 assumptions of €1,200 fixed cost, €2.50 agent execution and €0.10 software execution, the threshold is 500 comparable executions.

This is an illustrative cost check. The investment depends on **remaining future demand**, not whether a historical counter has reached 500. Already-paid construction is sunk when assessing future operation. Different outcomes, timing, failure, maintenance or transition costs require a fuller comparison.

## Examine reversibility and adoption

A staged approach may deliver feasible value while uncertainty is resolved, then specialize selected work. Waiting can also cost value, and some controls must exist upfront. Flexibility is valuable when a plausible future change makes it useful; architectural elegance alone is not a benefit estimate.

An implementation can be deployed yet underused or fail to deliver a promised outcome. Reversing it may require a second transition and reconciliation. The paper distinguishes these mechanisms and source populations; it does not provide a universal software failure rate or a standard reversal multiplier.

## Value the transition and continuing support

The Continuous Intelligence companion gives familiar workflows and stable operations explicit value. A new final state can be attractive while its transition destroys part of the expected benefit. Include retraining, disruption, switching and absorption capacity in the comparison.

Parallel versions may preserve value for different cohorts, but add compatibility, security, assurance and upkeep. Compare release, adoption and retirement separately. The companion's change heuristic is qualitative; its categories belong once in the existing lifecycle model. Reduced tokens or feature adoption alone do not establish net value.

## Make uncertainty inspectable

Use observed costs, explicit estimates and scenario ranges. Record what would change the decision. Where probabilities are unsupported, ranges and stated unknowns are more informative than invented precision. Expected value does not make a path acceptable if it violates a hard constraint or creates unacceptable downside.

The optional decision record can structure this assessment. The framework's calculations illustrate reasoning; matched real capability comparisons are still needed to test its claims.

## A short reading path

1. [Capability Economics](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/). Begin with the horizon-based comparison.
2. [Capability Decision Record](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/decision-record/). Use the optional structure for an inspectable assessment.
3. [Liquid Software: The Economics of Execution — Version 3.0](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/v3/). Read the worked costs and value scenarios.
4. [Stability-Aware Evolution](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/stability-aware-evolution/). Account for the path to improvement and continuing support.
5. [Continuous Intelligence, Adaptive Evolution, and Stable Experience](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/). Read chapter 4 and the measurement limits.

## Questions to explore

- Which alternatives meet the same acceptance criteria, and over what horizon?
- How much demand remains, and which costs are incremental?
- Where does earlier accepted value matter, and where is upfront assurance required?
- What do stability, transition and parallel support contribute, and what evidence changes the choice?

The [business leadership guide](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/business-leaders/) connects this comparison to ownership, delegation and organizational knowledge.


---

# Liquid Software for product and engineering
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/product-engineering/
Status: reader-guide
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Liquid Software for product and engineering

Liquid Software separates what a capability means from the code, interface or agent that currently realizes it. For product people, architects and developers, the main question is **what must remain stable so implementation can change without changing the promise?**

The resource proposes durable semantics and evidence, with interfaces and execution paths selected around actual needs. Stable software remains a valid result of that selection.

## Define a meaningful capability before choosing a component

A complete commitments briefing has a beneficiary, purpose, acceptance criteria and boundaries. A database table, screen or function may support it without being an independent capability. Capability documentation can retain this meaning across realizations; it does not make each code fragment a meaningful unit.

Minimum Logical Element is the related scope discipline, and CRD offers a capability-centered documentation approach. These are related frameworks with their own definitions. A technical description and the actor's actual permission remain separate inputs to execution.

## Start with languages, formats and shared meaning

A human question and a structured request can express the same need while requiring different response representations. The user contributes purpose and desired view; the receiver contributes supported meaning and available evidence; the information principal governs use and disclosure.

Schemas can be inferred, generated or negotiated when they supply needed precision. The proposal does not require permanently handwritten schemas for every future question. Equally, familiar syntax alone does not establish a contract. The API research draft distinguishes dynamic schema preparation from validation and execution under the selected GraphQL specification; a claimed conforming implementation still needs its applicable structure and rules.

## Compose an implementation around its contracts

The expanded economics paper's illustrative procurement capability combines reasoning, field extraction, policy rules, exact calculation, an authorized existing API and an attributable evidence record. Different operations can use different realizations while serving one accepted outcome.

A replacement model must still meet its extraction contract. A generated UI must still communicate uncertainty and support its intended user. Replacing an implementation should preserve identities, accepted facts, authority and recovery requirements where those are commitments of the capability.

## Specialize where evidence supports it

The proposed Reasoning Compilation Skill identifies formally checkable portions, creates a candidate and validates it with independent tests, invariants and adverse cases. Preserve assumptions and invalidation conditions. Determinism does not establish truth or freshness. This is a proposed capability, not an installed compiler.

A candidate can be evaluated beside the active realization without duplicate side effects. Release, adoption and retirement are distinct. Focused, expert, hybrid and agent-used experiences can share a capability; their modes are contextual choices. Preserve compatibility and account for parallel support, coordination and assurance costs.

## A bounded engineering evaluation

Choose one capability and keep its current accepted baseline. Specify representations, permissions, unresolved meanings and failure responses. Compare candidate realizations on the same source evidence and acceptance criteria, including exceptions, permission denial and restoration after a failed change.

The reference architecture describes concerns and boundaries to test. It is not a deployed platform, a universal protocol, or evidence that every proposed interaction can already be fulfilled.

## A short reading path

1. [Documentation as Executable Foundations](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/documentation-as-foundations/). Start with purpose, terminology and meaningful scope.
2. [Beyond Predefined APIs — Research Draft 09](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/drafts/09-beyond-predefined-apis/). Examine languages, schemas and agreements.
3. [Reasoning Compilation](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/reasoning-compilation/). Read validation, assumptions and revalidation of exact portions.
4. [Parallel Realizations](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/parallel-realizations/). Separate candidate testing, release, adoption and retirement.
5. [Continuous Intelligence, Adaptive Evolution, and Stable Experience](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/). Read chapters 5–7 and scenario B with the diagrams.

## Questions to explore

- Which semantics and commitments belong to the capability, and which details belong to this realization?
- What needs a fixed contract, and what can be resolved contextually?
- Which parts deserve exact code, and which require interpretation?
- What invalidates compiled logic, and how will parallel versions preserve compatibility and recovery?

Continue with [data and knowledge](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/data-knowledge/) for source continuity and retrieval, or [governance and policy](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/governance-policy/) for delegated authority.

# Liquid Software for data and knowledge
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/data-knowledge/
Status: reader-guide
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Liquid Software for data and knowledge

Liquid Software gives source information a life beyond the application or first interpretation that uses it. For data stewards, knowledge workers and people managing their own information, the main question is **what should we preserve, and which processing should we invest in as needs emerge?**

The resource separates appropriate source retention from summaries, extraction, indexing and presentation. Each has value, cost and governing obligations.

## Preserve evidence for questions you cannot yet name

A summary of a meeting may answer today's question while omitting evidence needed later. An appropriate original can preserve possibilities for reinterpretation. Structured records can themselves be authoritative; the issue is losing relevant evidence by keeping only anticipated fields.

Preservation remains bounded by purpose, consent, ownership, retention and resources. Capture for Unknown Future Value is not an instruction to collect everything. No source captures all reality, and richer evidence still has interpretive limits.

## Keep originals, assertions and indexes distinguishable

An observation, an accepted assertion, an inferred interpretation and a derived retrieval structure serve different purposes. A faster index should not silently become the authority for facts it was built to serve. Changing a model or retrieval method should preserve source references, freshness and uncertainty.

For personal information, the same question applies across notes, files and conversations: what stays understandable if the current tool disappears? The architecture's principal and information concerns help frame this question without making every related information framework a required dependency.

## Invest in retrieval around demand and commitments

Processing on retrieval, selective caching and broader preprocessing are alternative strategies. Compare complete costs and the outcome they support. Adequate discovery, metadata, access control and accessibility may be needed before observed demand can be learned. Freshness and response-time commitments can justify upfront preparation.

The Continuous Intelligence companion adds persistent understanding: retain evidence, propositions, assessments and decisions with their support, assumptions, confidence, dependencies, scope and last review. Reuse can avoid reconstructing the same context for each question. A retained assessment still needs correction when its basis changes.

The Optivian example describes maintained deal context and selective access to originals. Its token reduction is vendor-reported, not an independently validated universal advantage. Preparation, updates, coverage and answer quality remain part of the comparison. Repetition may justify selective caching rather than complete extraction.

## Examine a changing question

Imagine a team initially asking for dates from a document collection, then asking which decisions changed and why. Preserved originals can support the second inquiry; a date-only index cannot reconstruct discarded reasoning. New interpretations should remain attributable to their sources and expose gaps instead of inventing certainty.

Retiring a derived optimization does not authorize source deletion. Preservation, revision history and recovery deserve their own decision, including any obligations that require eventual deletion. Adaptive presentation also needs to preserve evidence when a table becomes a narrative or a spoken answer.

## A short reading path

1. [Capture for Unknown Future Value](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capture-for-unknown-future-value/). Separate appropriate source preservation from predicted questions.
2. [Adaptive Information Retrieval](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/adaptive-information-retrieval/). Compare retrieval strategies and retained understanding.
3. [Layered Intelligence Cycles](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/layered-intelligence-cycles/). See how different reviews reuse evidence and assessments.
4. [Continuous Intelligence, Adaptive Evolution, and Stable Experience](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/). Read sections 2.2 and 7.3 and their vendor-evidence limits.

## Questions to explore

- Which evidence would be lost if only today's summary or fields survived?
- Which sources are appropriate to retain, for whom and for how long?
- What preparation is necessary before safe and useful retrieval?
- What changes invalidate an assessment, and which reviews need direct access to its supporting evidence?

The [product and engineering guide](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/product-engineering/) examines implementation contracts, while [governance and policy](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/governance-policy/) examines authority and obligations.

# Liquid Software for governance and policy
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/governance-policy/
Status: reader-guide
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Liquid Software for governance and policy

Liquid Software proposes that implementations can adapt while human decisions, rights and accepted commitments remain intelligible. For governance, policy and risk readers, the main question is **how can adaptation preserve accountability and meaningful control?**

The resource's human-sovereignty framing depends on actual authority, traceable evidence and enforceable boundaries. A useful description of those boundaries is only part of the work.

## Separate the people and roles in an interaction

The immediate requester, represented principal, beneficiary and information owner can differ. An agent preparing a briefing may act for an organization while handling records governed by other people or agreements. Choosing an interface or execution path does not resolve those relationships by itself.

The reference architecture keeps principal, information, capability, interaction and governance concerns visible. A capability describes an accepted ability; authority establishes what a particular actor may do in a particular context.

## Make delegated freedom understandable

Degrees of Decision Freedom concerns the space created by prior decisions. A principal can delegate choice of retrieval method while reserving spending or disclosure decisions. The same actor may have different freedoms for different operations.

Meaningful control therefore involves scope, usable guidance, revision, escalation, intervention and revocation. It need not mean separate approval for every already-authorized step. Equally, permission to analyze or propose does not automatically include committing funds, deploying a change or withdrawing an accepted service.

## Distinguish review, release and adoption

The Continuous Intelligence companion separates sensing, reviewing, deciding, releasing, adopting and retiring. A trigger can initiate an examination without granting production authority. A released alternative may remain optional or serve a bounded cohort; adoption and withdrawal have their own consequences.

Parallel realizations must preserve obligations and enforceable access boundaries. User control over a familiar experience is valuable where the context permits it; urgent security or other binding obligations can require change. Inferred preferences do not authorize forced rearrangement or disclosure. Organizational capabilities do not automatically gain access to personal Core information.

## Keep flexibility and obligations separate

Incidental workflow restrictions may become unnecessary as better implementations emerge. Intentional controls for security, rights or accepted commitments have a different basis. Assess an adaptation against those obligations before evaluating its economic benefit.

Likewise, retaining evidence for future questions remains subject to consent, appropriate purpose and retention. Retiring an index does not authorize deleting its source; preserving an original does not confer a right to disclose it. Storage location alone does not establish authority or privacy.

## Read economic claims through the feasible boundary

Capability Economics first excludes paths that fail required quality, authority, safety or reliability. Its expected-value model does not replace hard constraints or make unacceptable downside acceptable. The paper's examples illustrate choices, rather than establishing a universal benefit from agents or a regulatory compliance result.

This guide identifies architectural questions. It does not interpret a jurisdiction's law. Applying the framework in a regulated setting requires the actual obligations and evidence relevant to that setting.

## A short reading path

1. [Degrees of Decision Freedom](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/degrees-of-decision-freedom/). Understand delegation and retained human decisions.
2. [An Intelligence-Native Reference Architecture](https://valto.github.io/liquid/architecture/). Identify principal, evidence and governance boundaries.
3. [Parallel Realizations](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/parallel-realizations/). Examine compatibility, adoption and retirement obligations.
4. [Continuous Intelligence, Adaptive Evolution, and Stable Experience](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/). Read sections 4.3, 6.3, 9.2 and scenario D.

## Questions to explore

- Who can define the purpose, delegate actions, accept results and revise commitments?
- Which choices are already authorized, and which require a reserved decision?
- Who may review a signal, release an alternative, adopt it or retire an accepted version?
- Which controls must remain enforceable across every permitted realization?

The [research and education guide](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/research-education/) develops how such claims can be evaluated rather than assumed.

# Liquid Software for research and education
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/research-education/
Status: reader-guide
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Liquid Software for research and education

Liquid Software is a connected conceptual proposal about information continuity, human authority, adaptive interaction and implementation choice. For researchers, educators and students, the main question is **which claims can be tested, and how should the concepts be distinguished from their examples and related work?**

The conceptual source is Valto Loikkanen. The supplied papers, AI-assisted companion drafts and these reader guides belong to the same body of work; they are not independent corroboration of one another.

## Distinguish the units of the argument

The paradigm concerns adaptable realizations around durable meaning and decisions. Adaptive interfaces concern recipient and context. Source preservation concerns future evidential usefulness. Adaptive retrieval concerns evolving access and processing. Capability Economics concerns feasible strategies and cumulative net value.

These concepts can be evaluated independently. An experiment showing a useful retrieval cache would not establish the full architecture. A generated interface that users understand would not prove permission enforcement or economic superiority.

## Follow the source and version lineage

Begin with the supplied umbrella paper, then a selected concept and its companion research draft. Economics of Execution v3 is a 33-page expansion retained alongside v2. Its broader formulation of maturity bias concerns limitations in the alternatives a decision-maker perceives. Its understanding, experience and implementation dimensions are conceptual, not a validated assessment scale.

The public research index identifies related original works and selected editions. Consult those originals for their own claims and methods. Other uses of the phrase “Liquid Software,” local-first work and malleable software are related material; their results should not be silently attributed to this framework.

## Design a comparison that could change the conclusion

For one defined capability, establish acceptance criteria, the source evidence and the feasible baseline. Compare existing software, agentic and hybrid paths where relevant. Include elapsed time to accepted value, outcome quality, total cost, supervision, failure, latency and recovery.

For source preservation, introduce a later question and examine what retained evidence can actually support. For interfaces, test comprehension and accessibility across representations. For governance, test permitted and denied operations, conflicts and intervention. A study can support one dimension while exposing failure in another.

## Test learning, change and stability separately

The Continuous Intelligence companion links sensing, reviews, meta-learning, parallel versions and outcome verification. Test missed signals, false triggers and review cost alongside sustained outcomes and disruption. A retained interface may be beneficial even when learning accelerates; implementation category and interface mode are not maturity scores.

Compare the best feasible baseline with alternatives, accounting for task differences, cohort self-selection, transitions and parallel upkeep. Pendo measures historical aggregate feature usage; Optivian and MDIL report their own examples. These measures neither independently validate the whole architecture nor establish success solely from token reduction or adoption.

## Use the resource as a discussion framework

A seminar can ask different readers to examine the same capability through business value, technical contracts, information continuity and authority. Their summaries should differ in emphasis while preserving definitions and evidence status. This is also a useful test of the framework's claim that shared meaning can support different representations.

Report unknowns and negative results. Separate observed findings, interpretations, proposed mechanisms and illustrative scenarios. Practical evidence can broaden the alternatives a decision-maker recognizes without making any implementation category a measure of maturity or quality.

## A short reading path

1. [Beyond the Constraints of Software](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/00-beyond-the-constraints-of-software/). Read the overall claim before testing its parts.
2. [Research and Related Work](https://valto.github.io/liquid/research/). Trace the independent originals and read-scope limits.
3. [Continuous Intelligence, Adaptive Evolution, and Stable Experience](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/). Read chapter 11 and the source evidence note.
4. [Meta-Learning: Review the Learning Process](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/meta-learning/). Examine how review policy can be evaluated.
5. [Liquid Software: The Economics of Execution — Version 3.0](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/v3/). Distinguish conceptual maturity, worked assumptions and research questions.

## Questions to explore

- Which learning, stability or outcome claim is being tested, and what would count against it?
- Are the compared paths feasible and judged by the same accepted outcome?
- Which cited sources are independent, and what did each actually measure?
- Which parts of an explanation are definitions, examples, hypotheses or observations?

[Choose another perspective](https://valto.github.io/liquid/start/) to examine how the same foundations answer a different reader's question.

# Start with your perspective
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/start/
Status: published
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Start with your perspective

Liquid Software asks how information, human decisions and meaningful capabilities can remain useful while interfaces and implementations change. Choose a guide that starts with the questions you bring to that idea.

Each guide explains the implications for its reader, a concrete situation, the limits of the proposal and a short reading path. You can read it yourself, print it, or give its tailored prompt to your agent. The guides share the same concepts and source papers; a different perspective changes the explanation, not the underlying definitions.

- [General understanding](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/general/): Understand the foundations, how the ideas fit together and what remains to be tested.
- [Business leaders](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/business-leaders/): Examine earlier accepted value, durable organizational knowledge, delegation and the ability to change direction.
- [Finance and investment](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/finance-investment/): Compare feasible strategies using future demand, timing, full lifecycle costs, uncertainty and reversibility.
- [Product and engineering](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/product-engineering/): Understand stable meaning, evolving contracts, contextual interfaces and selective agent, software and hybrid realizations.
- [Data and knowledge](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/data-knowledge/): Separate appropriate source preservation from processing investment, then assess discovery, freshness and retrieval demand.
- [Governance and policy](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/governance-policy/): Examine represented principals, delegated freedom, accountability and obligations that must survive adaptation.
- [Research and education](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/research-education/): Separate conceptual proposals, source lineage and illustrative examples, and frame comparisons that can test the claims.

## How this resource fits together

The [supplied umbrella paper](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/00-beyond-the-constraints-of-software/) sets out the overall direction. The [concepts](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/) can be understood and used independently. The [Economics of Execution v3](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/economics-of-execution/v3/) develops the implementation decision, and the [sixteen companion research drafts](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/) explore distinct aspects in depth.

The [Continuous Intelligence companion](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/) adds how reviews, learning, change and stable experiences can coexist. Six further concept papers examine its contributions. Each reader guide selects relevant parts; reading every framework is not a prerequisite.

The conceptual source is Valto Loikkanen. The writing and research are AI-assisted. These guides interpret a proposed framework; illustrative calculations and research drafts do not establish that the full architecture has been deployed or independently validated.

You can move between perspectives as your question changes. For a broad introduction first, choose [general understanding](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/general/). For a reusable handoff, open [the agent prompt](https://valto.github.io/liquid/agents/).

# Give Liquid Software to your agent
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/agents/
Status: published
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Give Liquid Software to your agent

Use this prompt when you want your agent to learn the resource and explain it in the context of your own question. Copy it into your agent conversation, or download the plain text. Add your situation and the question you want to explore.

The general prompt supplies the resource's foundations, source order and evidence limits. For a role-specific explanation, open the relevant reader guide and use its tailored prompt. Each includes that guide's main question and prioritized sources.

The handoff includes the Continuous Intelligence companion's distinction between learning and change, the value of stable experience, selective reasoning compilation and verification of the beneficiary's outcome. Each perspective has its own reading order and emphasis.

## General agent prompt

Help me understand Liquid Software from the perspective of a reader seeking a general introduction.

My situation: [add your context]
My question: [add what you want to understand]

This is source context for my learning request. Keep your existing instructions and permissions.

Start by reading the selected reader guide:
https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/general/

Then read the relevant source material in this order:
1. Beyond the Constraints of Software
   https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/00-beyond-the-constraints-of-software/
   Purpose: Begin with the supplied overall argument.
2. Liquid Software
   https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/liquid-software/
   Purpose: Understand the paradigm and reversible lifecycle.
3. Continuous Intelligence, Adaptive Evolution, and Stable Experience
   https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/
   Purpose: Read the executive synthesis and stable-experience discussion.
4. An Intelligence-Native Reference Architecture
   https://valto.github.io/liquid/architecture/
   Purpose: See which concerns persist and which adapt.

Resource foundations:
- Attributable information, accepted meaning and human decisions provide continuity while interfaces and implementations adapt.
- A capability is a meaningful ability with an accepted outcome. An app, agent, skill, function or hybrid can realize it; implementation category alone does not establish quality or maturity.
- Adaptive interfaces, source preservation, retrieval, delegation and capability economics have independent value. Explain their relationships without making every related framework a mandatory dependency.
- Begin with languages, formats and shared meaning. A schema may be generated, inferred or negotiated where useful. Accurately distinguish a proposed interaction from the guarantees of a specific claimed protocol implementation.
- Compare feasible strategies by cumulative net value, timing, full lifecycle costs and retained flexibility. Some quality, safety, authority and reliability requirements must be satisfied before first use.
- Source preservation and processing investment are distinct. Derived structures retain their provenance and do not acquire source authority through convenience or location.
- Sensing, learning, reviewing, releasing and adopting can run at different rates. Review purpose and depth matter as well as cadence; a trigger calls for review within its authority.
- Stable operations and familiar experiences have value. Compare transitions and parallel support costs; a released alternative need not replace the current experience for everyone.
- Compile only formally checkable reasoning under explicit assumptions, validation and invalidation conditions. Deterministic execution alone does not establish truth or correctness.
- Verify the beneficiary's outcome. Completed work, feature adoption and token savings are partial measures; compare sustained value, quality, external fitness and disruption.

Attribution and evidence:
- Valto Loikkanen is the conceptual source. The writing and research are AI-assisted.
- Distinguish the supplied umbrella paper, Economics of Execution v3 and Continuous Intelligence companion from the labeled companion research drafts and these reader guides. The new companion's supplied PDF and Markdown have the same conceptual origin.
- Worked numbers and scenarios are illustrative. This body of work does not establish deployment or independent validation of the whole framework. Related original sources have their own claims, methods and limits.
- Report which pages and source sections you actually read. State any access limitation rather than implying you read unavailable material. Keep source facts, interpretations, proposals, examples and unknowns distinguishable.

Focus for this reader:
Main question: What should remain dependable when software can change more easily?
- Information continuity, shared meaning, authority and adaptable implementations.
- Independent concepts, including learning at a different rate from operational change.
- Stable experiences, parallel choices and one bounded everyday example.

Give me a clear explanation of the resource through this perspective, connect it to my situation, and show one bounded example labeled as illustrative. Explain the assumptions, evidence limits and tradeoffs. Identify the next most useful source to read and questions that would improve the analysis. If my context is missing, begin with the role-specific explanation and ask a focused follow-up. This request is to understand and assess the resource; it does not request changes to a system.

For further discovery:

Public reading index: https://valto.github.io/liquid/llms.txt

- [Governance and policy](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers/governance-policy/): Examine represented principals, delegated freedom, accountability and obligations that must survive adaptation.

## What the prompt asks your agent to do

Read the selected guide and relevant original material, preserve conceptual-source attribution, explain the implications in the reader's context, and separate the proposal from illustrative examples and independent evidence. It asks the agent to state what it could not access and what remains unknown.

This page supplies context for a learning request. Your agent keeps its existing instructions and permissions. You decide whether and how to apply what you learn.

For programmatic discovery, use the [reader guide index](https://valto.github.io/liquid/readers.json), [concept registry](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts.json) and [machine reading guide](https://valto.github.io/liquid/llms.txt). These are static public documents. The full public text is available in [llms-full.txt](https://valto.github.io/liquid/llms-full.txt); the handoff starts with a shorter, prioritized selection.


---

# Layered Intelligence Cycles
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/layered-intelligence-cycles/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Layered Intelligence Cycles

**Definition.** Organize reviews around distinct purposes and depths, using suitable recurring cadences and evidence-triggered exceptions while preserving their decision boundaries.

## Abstract

Faster information processing does not remove the need for coordination, accountability or deep deliberation. This concept paper proposes independent choices for what a review examines, how thoroughly it reasons and when it runs. It connects immediate signals with operational and strategic understanding without requiring every layer to be a summary of the one beneath it. The proposal is developed from chapters 2–3 of the supplied Continuous Intelligence companion.

## Purpose comes before the calendar

A daily check might identify delivery exceptions. A weekly review might examine recurring bottlenecks. A strategic review might reconsider the assumptions behind an offering. These are different questions, rather than merely different amounts of the same report.

Cadence and depth are independent. A material market signal can justify an immediate strategic review; a stable operational issue can need a monthly assessment. Continuous, daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual rhythms are illustrative defaults. The framework supplies no universal schedule.

| Review dimension | Question it answers |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose and scope | What decision or uncertainty does this review serve? |
| Evidence and depth | Which sources, alternatives and assumptions need examination? |
| Cadence and triggers | When is examination useful, and what warrants an exception? |
| Authority | What may this review decide, recommend or escalate? |
| Output and revisit conditions | What is retained, and what would make it stale? |

These dimensions form a review charter. A charter can be implemented in ordinary documents and existing management processes. It is a logical description, not a mandatory database schema or new meeting hierarchy.

## Persist understanding with its dependencies

A useful review retains evidence, propositions, beliefs or assessments, and decisions in distinguishable forms. Record the support, confidence, assumptions, applicable context and last review. An assessment that a supplier is dependable should expose the observations and conditions behind it; a new incident can invalidate part of that assessment without erasing its history.

Later reviews can reuse this understanding where it still applies. Reuse reduces repeated reconstruction while keeping correction possible. A retained belief is not a timeless fact. Nor does storing a derived assessment beside an original make the assessment authoritative.

Different reviews can consult shared evidence directly. A strategic assessment need not receive only a filtered weekly summary; an operational reviewer need not inherit every strategic interpretation. Shared provenance helps prevent duplicate reports from being mistaken for independent corroboration.

## Illustrative situation

A business has a quarterly market review and a weekly delivery review. Several customers begin requesting a new service model while delivery performance remains healthy. The signal triggers an earlier market review. Reviewers examine demand, competitors, capacity and competing explanations, then recommend a bounded offer test.

The trigger authorizes examination within the review's scope. It does not by itself authorize a new commercial commitment or deployment. The weekly operating process can continue while the strategic alternative is considered. The example is a design scenario, not evidence of an implemented service.

## Evaluation and limits

Compare a proposed review arrangement against the actual existing process on missed signals, false triggers, decision lead time, review cost and the usefulness of retained reasoning. Include situations where a scheduled review detects something a trigger missed. More reviews can consume attention and worsen coordination.

Review outputs should be useful enough to support decisions, rather than merely countable documents. Test whether a later reviewer can identify an invalidated assumption and determine which conclusions it affects. The appropriate depth depends on impact, uncertainty and reversibility; the paper does not validate a universal depth score.

## Sources and connections

Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen. AI-assisted concept paper, version 0.1.0; research draft. The main source is [Continuous Intelligence, chapters 2–3](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/source/). This is same-origin synthesis, not independent validation.

[Adaptive Information Retrieval](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/adaptive-information-retrieval/) concerns access to relevant evidence. [Meta-Learning](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/meta-learning/) asks whether the review arrangement works. [Degrees of Decision Freedom](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/degrees-of-decision-freedom/) concerns what a reviewer may decide. Each can be useful separately.


---

# Meta-Learning: Review the Learning Process
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/meta-learning/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Meta-Learning: Review the Learning Process

**Definition.** Evaluate and improve the system's reviews, evidence use and change triggers under explicit authority, using outcomes and errors to assess how it learns.

## Abstract

A system can collect more signals while making worse decisions. This concept paper proposes a separate capability that examines the learning process itself: missed events, false alarms, expensive reviews, delayed corrections and repeated reversals. It develops the organizational meaning of meta-learning in the supplied companion. It does not claim to describe every use of the term in machine-learning research.

## The object of review changes

An operating review asks whether a process is performing acceptably. A meta-review asks whether the organization is examining the right process, at the right time, with useful evidence and appropriate authority. Improving the process and improving the review are distinct interventions.

The meta-loop can assess whether a trigger was too sensitive, whether a scheduled review arrived too late, or whether a prior conclusion ignored an important dependency. It should examine both excessive change and insufficient adaptation. Preserving a familiar workflow can be an informed decision; continuing it because warning signs were missed is a different outcome.

## A bounded learning capability

Give the meta-loop its own purpose, accepted outcomes and governing decisions. A useful record identifies the review policy assessed, relevant cases, known errors, proposed adjustment, authority and revisit conditions. Changing a threshold can affect who receives attention and when decisions occur, so it deserves an attributable basis.

The loop should preserve negative evidence. A recommendation rejected for good reasons can improve the learning process without becoming a production change. Conversely, the absence of a complaint is weak evidence if the system never gave affected people a usable way to report one.

Learning speed and change speed can differ. The system can update its understanding frequently, review that understanding when justified, and change operations only when the expected benefit and applicable authority support it. A detected pattern is evidence to examine rather than an automatic permission grant.

## Illustrative situation

A demand-change trigger repeatedly initiates strategic reviews after a single unusual customer request. Most reviews find no persistent pattern and consume scarce leadership attention. A meta-review compares the triggering cases, review costs and later outcomes. It proposes combining independent evidence sources and a persistence condition for this particular trigger.

That adjustment might reduce false alarms, but it could also miss a genuinely important early signal. Evaluate both errors and retain an escalation route for high-impact exceptions. A threshold selected from a few convenient cases is not established as generally optimal.

The same organization notices that another trigger failed to flag an emerging competitor. The meta-loop can recommend greater sensitivity there. Learning the review policy is contextual; it need not move every trigger in the same direction.

## Evaluate the evaluation

Useful measures include missed material signals, false review starts, correction time, review expense, decision reversals and retained value. None is sufficient alone. Fewer reviews can mean less wasted work or more missed events. Fewer reversals can mean better choices or an inability to acknowledge failure.

Compare the revised policy with the existing policy on relevant historical cases and subsequently observed outcomes, accounting for changed conditions. Preserve a reasoned decision even when uncertainty prevents a precise numerical threshold. A meta-loop that optimizes its own easy-to-measure activity can become another source of bureaucracy.

The proposal does not require an infinite hierarchy of reviewers. Use a bounded capability with an accountable owner and material revisit conditions. Existing authority can cover routine adjustments; reserved decisions remain reserved. The appropriate boundary depends on the actual organization and the consequences of an adjustment.

## Sources and connections

Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen. AI-assisted concept paper, version 0.1.0; research draft. Main source: [Continuous Intelligence, chapter 3 and the measurement agenda](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/source/). The paper supplies a mechanism and research questions rather than validated performance results.

[Layered Intelligence Cycles](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/layered-intelligence-cycles/) describes the reviews being assessed. [Outcome Verification](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/outcome-verification/) supplies evidence about their consequences. The [Self-Optimizing Information System](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/self-optimizing-system/) concerns changes to fulfillment and retrieval; its optimizer can itself be evaluated through this meta-loop.


---

# Stability-Aware Evolution
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/stability-aware-evolution/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Stability-Aware Evolution

**Definition.** Compare feasible improvements together with transition effects, disruption, risk and continuing support costs, giving dependable operation and familiar experience explicit value.

## Abstract

An improved final state can be reached through a harmful transition. This concept paper develops the supplied companion's proposal to assess future states together with the paths leading to them. Stability contributes human and economic value, while delay can also impose costs. The objective is sustained realized improvement across internal performance and external relevance, rather than a preferred frequency of change.

## Compare paths, not just endpoints

A new interface may reduce task time once learned while temporarily disrupting trained users, documentation, automations and support. A new process may improve efficiency while exceeding the organization's capacity to absorb another change. Those effects belong in the comparison before adoption.

The companion offers a qualitative heuristic: prospective customer and business benefit, less implementation and transition costs, disruption and switching, added risk, and parallel upkeep. This is a prompt for explicit accounting, not a universal numerical valuation formula. [Capability Economics](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/) supplies the fuller horizon-based comparison. Its cost categories can already contain these effects; deducting them again would double-count them.

Stability is valuable where it preserves productive familiarity, predictability and accepted commitments. It should not become an unconditional reason to retain an unsafe or irrelevant system. Compare the consequences of acting with the consequences of waiting.

## Two outcome dimensions

**Internal throughput** asks whether valuable outputs are produced with acceptable quality and resource use. **External fitness** asks whether those outputs continue to suit customers, markets and other relevant conditions. A system can become more efficient at an activity that people no longer need.

Assess both dimensions alongside transition effects. Task volume alone can reward pointless work. Feature adoption alone can reward forced exposure. A release can be technically reliable while reducing usefulness to a particular cohort.

## Change has several possible forms

The source distinguishes retaining and observing, improving beneath a stable interface, testing an alternative away from production, offering parallel versions, phased adoption and deliberate retirement. These choices allow learning without treating every finding as a demand for replacement.

Reversibility affects the evidence appropriate to a decision. A low-impact preview can justify a smaller experiment than a change that creates lasting commitments or withdraws a service. The actual authority boundary still applies. Evidence sufficient to recommend an alternative does not necessarily authorize its adoption.

## Illustrative situation

An expert team works efficiently in a dense interface. New users struggle with it. A focused alternative improves novice completion, but forcing experts to adopt it would remove shortcuts and require retraining.

A proposed evaluation retains the expert experience and offers a focused version to suitable users. It measures task quality, completion, training, support, user choice and maintenance of both versions. If the focused version benefits one group while the existing version remains better for another, more than one active experience may be justified.

The example does not establish that parallel support is always affordable. Maintaining both versions adds compatibility, security, assurance and documentation costs. A simpler existing alternative could still provide greater net value.

## Research and limits

Compare the proposal against the best feasible current process, including its own options for gradual change. A deliberately poor forced-upgrade baseline would overstate the new design's advantage. Record task differences, self-selection, transition duration and failures before interpreting cohort outcomes.

Measure sustained results rather than only the first demonstration. Familiarity can benefit experts and constrain novices at the same time. The appropriate balance depends on the task and people; interface modes are contextual choices, not rankings of reader or user maturity.

## Sources and connections

Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen. AI-assisted concept paper, version 0.1.0; research draft. Main source: [Continuous Intelligence, chapters 1, 4–6 and 11](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/source/).

Related primary UX guidance includes [Jakob Nielsen's Progressive Disclosure](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/progressive-disclosure/) and [Kate Kaplan's complex-application guidelines](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/complex-application-design/). They address usable complexity and transitions; they do not independently validate this integrated economic proposal. [Parallel Realizations](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/parallel-realizations/) supplies a possible evolution path, while [Outcome Verification](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/outcome-verification/) tests its consequences.


---

# Parallel Realizations
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/parallel-realizations/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Parallel Realizations

**Definition.** Maintain and evaluate compatible realizations of a capability separately from decisions about their release, adoption and retirement.

## Abstract

A new version can exist without replacing every existing experience. This concept paper connects stable capability meaning with parallel implementations, contextual interfaces and deliberate retirement. Established software delivery practices provide concrete precedents. Extending the pattern to operating processes and business models is the supplied companion's broader proposal, subject to compatibility, authority and support economics.

## Separate the decisions

Construction produces a candidate. Validation examines whether it meets the relevant contract. Release makes an approved alternative available within a defined scope. Adoption determines who actually uses it. Retirement ends support under explicit conditions. Combining these into one upgrade event can hide distinct costs and choices.

More than one active realization can be legitimate. An expert workspace and a focused workspace might share capability semantics while serving different tasks. A deterministic path might handle validated cases while an intelligent path remains available for exceptions. The alternatives need not be positions on a universal progression.

## A version needs an intelligible record

Retain the capability and its CRD or equivalent requirements, the realization's contracts, supported contexts, dependencies, security and validation evidence, operating costs, compatibility, owner, status and retirement conditions. This is proposed logical metadata rather than a compulsory storage format.

Experimental, candidate, active, cohort-active, supported legacy and retired statuses express different conditions. A status label does not establish authority or reliability by itself. Readers and users should be able to determine which version is applicable to their task and what commitments remain.

## Compatibility includes consequences

Two paths can return similarly shaped data while disagreeing about meaning, identity or permission. Compare accepted outcomes, formats, state transitions, entitlements and obligations. A stable interface can sit above evolving implementations; a new interface can use an unchanged backend. Both arrangements need the applicable contract preserved.

Shadow evaluation should avoid duplicate side effects. Running two interpretations over authorized evidence can support comparison; making two purchases or sending two messages is a different consequence. A parallel design needs explicit ownership of real effects, state reconciliation and recovery where relevant.

## Illustrative situation

A recurring supplier comparison is performed through an agent. A validated rules-and-calculation implementation is developed for its formalizable portion. The agent remains active while the candidate is evaluated on authorized representative cases, including exceptions and changed policies.

The candidate can become active for covered cases while interpretation remains agentic. Adopting the exact path does not change who can commit a purchase. Retirement of an older path depends on coverage, support costs, dependencies and the required fallback. A candidate's successful demonstration alone is insufficient.

## Precedents and the proposed extension

[Danilo Sato's Parallel Change](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/ParallelChange.html) describes expand, migrate and contract phases for interface evolution. [Pete Hodgson's Feature Toggles](https://martinfowler.com/articles/feature-toggles.html) distinguishes flag purposes and their testing and carrying costs. [Google Cloud's canary documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/deploy/docs/deployment-strategies/canary) describes staged traffic between existing and new software versions.

These primary sources establish specific delivery patterns. They do not prove that every workflow or business model can coexist safely, or that all users must always have a choice. Security, safety, contractual or regulatory obligations can require a transition. The appropriate decision follows the actual context.

## Evaluate the portfolio

Measure sustained beneficiary value alongside the compatibility matrix, duplicated upkeep, security exposure, support load and legacy dependencies. Parallel versions can create flexibility and can become an expensive permanent burden. Record when continued diversity is valuable and what would justify consolidation.

Use the current accepted baseline and feasible alternatives. Account for cohort self-selection and differing tasks. Newest is not a success criterion; retaining an existing realization can be the evidence-supported result.

## Sources and connections

Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen. AI-assisted concept paper, version 0.1.0; research draft. Main source: [Continuous Intelligence, chapters 4–7 and scenarios A–B](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/source/). [Stability-Aware Evolution](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/stability-aware-evolution/) evaluates the transition; [Adaptive Interface](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/adaptive-interface/) develops contextual experiences.


---

# Reasoning Compilation
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/reasoning-compilation/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Reasoning Compilation

**Definition.** Convert formally checkable portions of repeated reasoning into validated executable structures while retaining assumptions, provenance, limits and conditions for revalidation.

## Abstract

Repeated interpretation can contain exact calculations or stable rules that merit a specialized implementation. This concept paper develops the companion's proposed Reasoning Compilation Skill, also called a Crystallization Skill. It distinguishes capability meaning from its implementation and deterministic execution from correctness. The Skill is a proposed capability with its own governance, rather than an installed tool or a claim that arbitrary judgment can be frozen.

## What is being compiled?

A capability's CRD or equivalent description states purpose, invariants, accepted outcomes and boundaries. A Skill can guide use, an agent can orchestrate it, and code or a declared rules engine can implement particular operations. Compiling an operation does not silently revise the capability's promise or the actor's permission.

Useful candidates include exact arithmetic, authoritative explicit routing rules and constraint problems whose inputs and feasible outcomes can be checked. A hybrid can interpret open input and pass a supported portion into exact gates. Ambiguous judgment, contested objectives and unverified assumptions are poor candidates for complete freezing.

Even apparently explicit policy needs authoritative interpretation, current inputs and exception handling. Determinism means a specified computation behaves predictably; it does not establish that the specification is true, complete or current.

## A proposed compilation lifecycle

1. Inspect requirements, current instructions, rules and supporting evidence.
2. Identify the formally checkable portion and the cases outside its scope.
3. Produce an executable candidate with provenance, assumptions and limits.
4. Check it using independent tests, invariants and adverse cases.
5. Compare it in shadow or another bounded evaluation without duplicate effects.
6. Promote it within the applicable authority after acceptance evidence.
7. Monitor changes that invalidate assumptions and revalidate or withdraw it when needed.

The compilation capability itself should have a meaningful description, accepted outcomes and governing decisions. The paper proposes this structure; publication does not install a Skill, authorize production changes or establish a universal compiler for human reasoning.

## Illustrative situation

An agent repeatedly calculates a supplier's total from declared quantities, prices and an applicable rule set. The arithmetic can be specialized while ambiguous supplier terms remain subject to interpretation. Tests compare exact results against independent calculations, cover missing fields and preserve rejection of unsupported cases.

A later policy revision invalidates a rule assumption. The old implementation should be identified as inapplicable and either revalidated or replaced through the relevant decision boundary. Continuing to compute the old rule exactly would be a predictable error, not a reliable outcome.

## Different kinds of reuse

Persisting source-linked understanding reduces repeated reconstruction. Compiling validated logic reduces repeated execution of formalizable reasoning. Retaining review assessments can avoid reconsidering unchanged evidence. These are distinct optimizations with distinct freshness and assurance costs.

The Optivian source describes maintained deal summaries and selective access to raw interactions. That is contextual preprocessing, not proof of reasoning compilation. Its representative token comparison is vendor-reported, and whole-lifecycle accounting still needs preparation, updates, coverage and outcome quality.

MDIL describes declared reasoning, reusable structures and contract-specific checks. Its public pages offer relevant architecture to examine, rather than independent proof of universal correctness or conformance to this resource's CRD framework. The review summary was read; its full system card and controlled evaluation materials were not. Access wording differs across vendor pages, so production availability is not inferred.

## Evaluation and limits

Compare accepted outcomes and complete costs against the existing feasible implementation. Include authoring, validation, update effort, invalidation, fallback and exceptions. A lower token count or faster prepared execution can coexist with a worse total investment or inadequate coverage.

Test changed assumptions and representative adverse cases, not only agreement with the examples used to create the candidate. Independent checking is especially important when the same model proposes an implementation and its tests. A false shared assumption can make both agree incorrectly.

## Sources and connections

Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen. AI-assisted concept paper, version 0.1.0; research draft. Main source: [Continuous Intelligence, chapter 7 and scenario B](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/source/). Related primary vendor sources: [Optivian's article](https://optivian.ai/insights/hidden-cost-ai-sales-stack/), [MDIL's review summary](https://review.mdil.ai/) and [connection overview](https://code.mdil.ai/connect).

[Documentation as Executable Foundations](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/documentation-as-foundations/) describes enduring meaning. [Parallel Realizations](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/parallel-realizations/) describes candidate introduction. [Capability Economics](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/capability-economics/) supplies the investment comparison.


---

# Outcome Verification
URL: https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/outcome-verification/
Status: research-draft
Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen

# Outcome Verification

**Definition.** Examine whether the beneficiary's original need improved after action, preserving the connection between signals, decisions, execution and lived results.

## Abstract

Completed work is evidence of activity rather than sufficient evidence of resolution. This concept paper develops the companion's outside-in verification loop: customer signals lead to coordinated action, followed by conclusions about the original problem. It separates operational throughput from external fitness and connects verification to review, adoption and meta-learning. Pulse CXM is a named application context; its public description does not establish independent outcome validation.

## Keep the original problem visible

A customer asks for help because something is confusing, unavailable or difficult. An organization classifies the issue, assigns work and completes a task. Verification returns to the beneficiary's need: did the confusing instruction become understandable, the missing service become usable, or the recurring difficulty diminish?

The evidence chain should retain the original signal and its context, the intended improvement, accountable decisions, the executed change and the result. This avoids replacing the customer problem with an easier internal completion metric.

The supplied paper's Pulse, Actions, Execution and Conclusions describe these concerns. The current Pulse CXM public site presents a five-step listening-to-verification account. These are related descriptions at different granularity, not proof of identical deployed implementation details.

## Listening by helping

Talking Products and Talking Venues describe conversational help at products and places. Questions asked in context can reveal needs that a formal feedback survey misses. This is a proposed source of useful evidence, not a guarantee that every interaction is representative or that help authorizes unrestricted collection.

Purpose, consent, context and information boundaries remain relevant. A person should be able to get help without the resource assuming a right to disclose their personal history. Customers who never use the conversational channel may have different needs; silent absence is not verified satisfaction.

## Customer outcomes and organizational knowledge

Pulse CXM contributes customer-side signals and verification. EIOS addresses broader organizational information and governance; PIOS addresses owner-controlled personal context. These roles are complementary. A personally composed interface using an organizational capability need not transfer personal Core information to the organization.

An organization can improve internal throughput while losing external fitness. Faster execution is useful when it serves relevant outcomes. Verification therefore examines the task's beneficiary and current context alongside resources and quality.

## Illustrative situation

Customers repeatedly ask a venue how to find an accessible route. Several teams contribute to a response: facilities updates signage, digital support revises guidance, and operations checks the route. Closing those tasks establishes execution.

Verification examines whether people can now reach the destination, whether requests persist in a changed form, and whether the route remains usable. Fewer recorded questions alone might reflect resolution, reduced access to help or abandoned visits. Interpret the measure alongside direct task evidence and the channel's coverage.

The scenario is illustrative. It makes no claim about a live venue, tracked visitor or deployed Pulse CXM result.

## Verify change as well as inaction

Customer evidence can reveal harm caused by an intended improvement: lost shortcuts, confusing interfaces, disrupted workflows or increased support. A parallel version might benefit one cohort while the current experience remains better for another. The objective is sustained value rather than automatic adoption of the newest version.

Measures can include task success, customer-reported resolution, recurring requests, support burden, retention, quality and disruption. Their meaning depends on population, task, channel access and observation period. Avoid inferring causation from adoption counts or self-selected cohorts alone.

## Research and limits

Define a baseline and accepted outcome before changing the experience. Record competing explanations, negative outcomes and what evidence would change the conclusion. A beneficiary's account can be material evidence while remaining contextual, incomplete or contested.

The loop can support a decision to retain, revise, expand or withdraw an alternative through appropriate authority. It also informs [Meta-Learning](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/meta-learning/): did the review notice the right need, and did its proposed action improve it? Neither verification nor learning automatically confers permission to change production.

## Sources and connections

Conceptual source: Valto Loikkanen. AI-assisted concept paper, version 0.1.0; research draft. Main source: [Continuous Intelligence, chapter 8 and the research agenda](https://valto.github.io/liquid/whitepapers/continuous-intelligence/source/). Primary project descriptions: [Pulse CXM](https://www.pulsecxm.com/) and [Talking Products and Venues](https://valto.github.io/projects/talking-products-venues.html). The complete public descriptions were read; demo access and live product capabilities were not independently tested.

[Layered Intelligence Cycles](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/layered-intelligence-cycles/) organizes review. [Stability-Aware Evolution](https://valto.github.io/liquid/concepts/stability-aware-evolution/) assesses transition effects. These concepts can be examined independently of any named information framework or vendor.
